product_ja:
妙高産コシヒカリ（特別栽培米）
妙高連峰から流れ出す冷たい雪解け水と、高原特有の激しい寒暖差。この過酷な環境こそが、お米に圧倒的な「甘み」と「粘り」を蓄えさせます。炊き上がりの一粒一粒が直立し、眩いばかりに輝く姿は、まさに雪国の宝石。おかずなしで、まずはそのまま噛み締めてください。妙高の大地そのものを食べているような、力強い生命力を感じます。
product_en:
Koshihikari from Myoko (specially cultivated rice)
The cold meltwater flowing from the Myoko Mountain Range and the extreme temperature differences unique to the plateau. This harsh environment is what gives the rice its overwhelming sweetness and stickiness. The sight of each grain standing upright and shining brightly after cooking is truly a jewel of the snow country. Please enjoy it as is without any side dishes. You can feel the powerful vitality of the food, as if you were eating the very land of Myoko.
product_fr:
Koshihikari de Myoko (riz spécialement cultivé)
L'eau de fonte froide s'écoulant de la chaîne de montagnes Myoko et les différences de température extrêmes propres au plateau. C’est cet environnement hostile qui donne au riz son caractère incroyablement sucré et collant. La vue de chaque grain debout et brillant après la cuisson est véritablement un joyau du pays des neiges. Veuillez le déguster tel quel sans aucun accompagnement. Vous pouvez ressentir la puissante vitalité de la nourriture, comme si vous mangiez la terre même de Myoko.
product_tw:
妙高的越光（特產稻米）
從妙高山脈流淌的寒冷融水和高原特有的極端溫差。這種嚴酷的環境賦予了大米壓倒性的甜味和粘性。煮熟後一顆顆直立、閃閃發光的景象，真是雪國的一顆明珠。請直接享用，不加任何配菜。你可以感受到食物強大的生命力，就好像你正在吃妙高的土地一樣。

text_en: Kitarai. It is a simple station that stands alone in a vast rural landscape and is quietly enjoyed by commuting students and local residents. Although there are no large-scale station buildings in the area, the golden ears of rice that change color with the seasons and the vast silver landscape are full of the atmosphere that makes you feel close to the vastness of the Echigo Plain and the activities of agriculture. It quietly teaches us that the ordinary scene of waiting for the train to arrive on an unadorned platform is actually the real pleasure of the most luxurious train journey.

product_ja:
とん一の「とん漬け（越後味噌漬け）」
地元で愛される精肉店がつくる、新潟県産豚の味噌漬け。厳選された厚切りのロース肉を、地元の香り高い越後味噌にじっくりと漬け込んでいます。フライパンで焼けば、味噌の焦げる香ばしい香りが食欲を激しく刺激。柔らかな身から溢れる肉汁と味噌のコクが合わさり、ご飯が何杯でも進みます。北新井の家庭の味を、ぜひ食卓へ。
product_en:
Tonichi's "Tonzuke (Echigo Miso Pickled)"
Niigata prefecture pork marinated in miso, made by a locally loved butcher shop. Carefully selected thick-sliced ​​loin meat is carefully marinated in local fragrant Echigo miso. If you fry it in a frying pan, the fragrant aroma of burning miso will stimulate your appetite. The juiciness of the tender meat and the richness of the miso combine to go well with multiple bowls of rice. Please bring the taste of Kitaarai's home cooking to your table.
product_fr:
"Tonzuke (Echigo Miso mariné)" de Tonichi
Porc de la préfecture de Niigata mariné au miso, fabriqué par une boucherie appréciée localement. La viande de longe en tranches épaisses soigneusement sélectionnée est soigneusement marinée dans du miso Echigo parfumé local. Si vous le faites frire dans une poêle, l'arôme parfumé du miso brûlant stimulera votre appétit. La jutosité de la viande tendre et la richesse du miso se marient bien avec plusieurs bols de riz. S'il vous plaît, apportez le goût de la cuisine maison de Kitaarai à votre table.
product_tw:
東一的“越後味噌醃製”
新潟縣豬肉用味噌醃製，由當地一家深受喜愛的肉店製作。嚴選厚片腰肉，用當地香濃的越後味噌精心醃製。如果用平底鍋煎的話，味噌燒焦的芳香會刺激食慾。肉質的鮮嫩多汁和味噌的濃鬱，與多碗米飯相得益彰。請把北荒井家常菜的味道帶到您的餐桌上。

text_en: Joetsu Myoko. It used to be a simple small station called Wakinoda, standing alone in a rice field. Its appearance changed completely with the opening of the Hokuriku Shinkansen, and now a sophisticated, modern station building stands tall as the southern gateway to Niigata Prefecture. However, if you take a step outside the Shinkansen platform, you will see the unaltered majestic mountain range of Kubiki Sanzan, which seems to be quietly preserving the memory of the former Shin-Etsu Main Line. At SAKURA Plaza inside the station, travelers are welcomed with local sake and specialty products, and even amidst the new bustle, you can feel the weight of the history and warm love that this area has nurtured.

This land, which was once a rural area, expanded into a city with the rapid economic growth of the Showa era, and has played a role as a familiar means of transportation to support people's lives. At dusk, listening to the lively laughter of students coming down to the platform and looking out at the Myoko mountains in the distance, you can quietly feel the preciousness of everyday life and the breath of the city that has been passed down through the ages.

text_en: Takada. Located near Takada Castle Ruins Park, which is considered one of Japan's top three night cherry blossoms, it is a town rich in atmosphere with the elegance of a castle town and the series of ``gangi'' that are unique to snowy regions. During the Showa era, travelers were welcomed by a magnificent wooden station building, and in winter, the sound of geta walking on the streets covered in deep snow echoed pleasantly. The appearance of Sekaikan, one of the oldest movie theaters in Japan that still stands today, and the 4,000 cherry blossom trees that bloom with the arrival of spring are filled with beauty that continues to captivate the hearts of visitors and can be called the pride of Echigo.

product_ja:
武蔵野酒造「スキー正宗」
日本スキー発祥の地・高田。明治時代、オーストリアのレルヒ少佐にちなんで命名されたこの酒は、高田の「雁木（がんぎ）」の街並みのように、奥深くもスッキリとしたキレが自慢です。ほのかな花の香りと、雪解け水のような透明感。お取り寄せで人気のセットは、歴史の重みとモダンなセンスが融合した、高田の美意識を感じる一本です。
product_en:
Musashino Sake Brewery “Ski Masamune”
Takada, the birthplace of Japanese skiing. This sake, named after the Austrian Major Lerch during the Meiji period, boasts a deep yet refreshing taste, just like the streets of Gangi in Takada. A faint floral scent and a clarity similar to melting snow. The set, which is popular on order, is a piece that embodies Takada's aesthetic sense, which combines the weight of history with modern sensibilities.
product_fr:
Brasserie de saké Musashino « Ski Masamune »
Takada, berceau du ski japonais. Ce saké, nommé d'après le major autrichien Lerch de l'époque Meiji, possède un goût profond et rafraîchissant, à l'image des rues de Gangi à Takada. Un léger parfum floral et une clarté semblable à la fonte des neiges. L'ensemble, populaire sur commande, est une pièce qui incarne le sens esthétique de Takada, qui combine le poids de l'histoire avec les sensibilités modernes.
product_tw:
武藏野清酒釀造所“滑雪道地”
高田，日本滑雪運動的發源地。這款清酒以明治時期奧地利少校勒赫的名字命名，口感深沉而清爽，就像高田的甘義街道一樣。淡淡的花香和類似融化的雪的透明度。這套裝深受訂單歡迎，體現了高田的美學意識，將歷史的厚重與現代的感性結合。

audio_ja: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saffron12safron-oss/rail-audio/main/audio/妙高はねうまライン_妙高はねうまライン_10_ja.mp3
text_en: Kasugayama. With Kasugayama Castle, the residence of the famous Sengoku period warlord Kenshin Uesugi, in the background, it is a place that bears the weight of Echigo's history. Even when traveling by train in the Showa era, the ruggedness of the mountain castles seen from the train window greatly stimulated the imagination of travelers and made them think about the footsteps of military commanders who lived righteously. The parade for the Kenshin Festival held every August still fills the city with excitement, and although the surrounding scenery has been modernized, the dignified atmosphere felt in the breeze proves that the public spirit is still alive in this area.

product_ja:
かなざわ総本舗「出陣餅（しゅつじんもち）」
上杉謙信公の居城、春日山。戦場へ向かう将兵に餅を与えた故事にちなむこの銘菓は、風味豊かなよもぎ餅に、たっぷりのきな粉と黒蜜をかけていただきます。一口含めば、爽やかなよもぎの香りが鼻を抜け、上品な甘さが広がります。謙信公の「義」の心を今に伝える、上越を代表する歴史の味。個包装で届くため、お配り物にも最適です。
product_en:
Kanazawa Sohonpo “Shutsujinmochi”
Kasugayama, the residence of Uesugi Kenshin. This famous confection is named after a story where mochi was given to soldiers on their way to the battlefield, and is a richly flavored mugwort mochi topped with plenty of soybean flour and brown sugar syrup. When you take a sip, the refreshing scent of mugwort passes through your nose, and the elegant sweetness spreads out. A taste of history representing Joetsu that conveys Kenshin's spirit of righteousness to the present day. They arrive individually wrapped, making them ideal for handing out.
product_fr:
Kanazawa Sohonpo « Shutsujinmochi »
Kasugayama, la résidence d'Uesugi Kenshin. Cette célèbre confiserie doit son nom à une histoire selon laquelle le mochi était offert aux soldats en route vers le champ de bataille. Il s'agit d'un mochi à l'armoise richement parfumé, garni de beaucoup de farine de soja et de sirop de cassonade. Lorsque vous prenez une gorgée, le parfum rafraîchissant de l'armoise passe par votre nez et la douceur élégante se répand. Un avant-goût de l'histoire représentant Joetsu qui transmet l'esprit de droiture de Kenshin jusqu'à nos jours. Ils arrivent emballés individuellement, ce qui les rend idéaux pour être distribués.
product_tw:
金澤總本舖“酒神餅”
春日山，上杉謙信的宅邸。這種著名的甜點因在上戰場時送給士兵麻糬的故事而得名，是一種味道濃鬱的艾草麻糬，上面撒滿了大量的黃豆粉和紅糖糖漿。喝一口，清爽的艾草香味穿過鼻腔，淡雅的甜味擴散開來。代表上越的歷史味道，將劍心的正義精神傳達到了今天。它們是單獨包裝的，非常適合分發。

audio_ja: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saffron12safron-oss/rail-audio/main/audio/妙高はねうまライン_妙高はねうまライン_11_ja.mp3
text_en: Naoetsu. It was once a strategic railway hub where the Shinetsu Main Line and Hokuriku Main Line intersected, and it is truly a railway town, with the smell of coal and train whistles mingled in the sea breeze. Many railroad tracks run through the vast grounds, and the bustling atmosphere of the past, when the voices of vendors selling the famous ``taimeshi'' echoed through the platform, is still etched in the hearts of many railway fans. As the sun sets over the Sea of ​​Japan, painting the station building red, the sight of the lights of passing trains illuminating the tracks makes you feel deeply the countless lives that have been carried by railways and the depth of history that this seaside town has woven.

product_ja:
平八かまぼこ店「直江津名産 蒲鉾セット」
北前船の寄港地として栄えた港町・直江津で、大正時代から続く伝統の味。日本海の新鮮な魚を使い、石臼で丁寧に練り上げた蒲鉾は、驚くほどプリッとした弾力と、噛むほどに溢れる魚の旨味が別格です。保存料を極力抑え、素材本来の味を活かした「本物の蒲鉾」。直江津の潮風を感じながら、わさび醤油で贅沢に楽しみたい逸品です。
product_en:
Heihachi Kamaboko Store “Naoetsu Specialty Kamaboko Set”
A traditional taste that has continued since the Taisho era in Naoetsu, a port town that prospered as a port of call for Kitamaebune ships. Using fresh fish from the Sea of ​​Japan and carefully kneaded in a stone mill, the kamaboko has an amazingly firm elasticity and the flavor of the fish that overflows with every bite. "Genuine kamaboko" uses as little preservatives as possible and brings out the original taste of the ingredients. This is a delicacy that you want to enjoy luxuriously with wasabi and soy sauce while feeling the sea breeze of Naoetsu.
product_fr:
Magasin Heihachi Kamaboko « Ensemble Kamaboko spécialisé Naoetsu »
Un goût traditionnel qui perdure depuis l'ère Taisho à Naoetsu, une ville portuaire qui prospérait comme port d'escale des navires Kitamaebune. Fabriqué à partir de poisson frais de la mer du Japon et soigneusement pétri dans un moulin en pierre, le kamaboko possède une élasticité étonnamment ferme et la saveur du poisson qui déborde à chaque bouchée. Le « Véritable kamaboko » utilise le moins de conservateurs possible et fait ressortir le goût original des ingrédients. C'est un délice que l'on souhaite savourer luxueusement avec du wasabi et de la sauce soja tout en sentant la brise marine de Naoetsu.
product_tw:
平八魚糕店“直江津特產魚糕套餐”
作為北前船停靠港而繁榮的港口城市直江津，自大正時代以來一直延續的傳統味道。使用來自日本海的新鮮魚，在石磨中精心揉製而成的魚糕具有驚人的緊實彈性，每一口都溢出魚的香味。 「正宗魚糕」盡可能少使用防腐劑，最大限度地發揮食材的本來味道。一邊感受直江津的海風，一邊享受芥末和醬油的奢華美味。

text_en: Naoetsu. Once a strategic location where the Shinetsu Main Line and Hokuriku Main Line crossed, it is a town where the sound of train whistles blends into the sea breeze. It has prospered as a port town since ancient times, and the tranquility of Gochi Kokubunji still conveys the weight of history. Nowadays, the railway has been operated by the third sector, and the hustle and bustle of the past has calmed down, but the vast number of lines running parallel to each other still makes you feel the glory of the railway.

product_ja:
上越銘菓 笹飴（ささあめ）
夏目漱石の『坊っちゃん』にも登場した、歴史ある上越の名物。乾燥させた笹の葉に、純粋な米飴を挟んだ素朴なお菓子です。口に含めば、笹の清々しい香りと、米本来の優しい甘みがゆっくりと溶け出します。噛み締めるほどに懐かしく、時間が止まるような穏やかなひととき。港町・直江津が守り続けてきた、雪国の知恵と伝統を感じる逸品です。
product_en:
Joetsu famous confectionery Sasaame
A historic Joetsu specialty that was featured in Natsume Soseki's ``Botchan.'' It is a simple sweet made by sandwiching pure rice candy between dried bamboo leaves. When you put it in your mouth, the refreshing scent of bamboo and the gentle sweetness of rice slowly melt away. It's a peaceful moment that makes you feel so nostalgic that time seems to stop. This is a masterpiece where you can feel the wisdom and tradition of the snowy country that the port town of Naoetsu has continued to protect.
product_fr:
Joetsu célèbre confiserie Sasaame
Une spécialité historique de Joetsu qui figurait dans le « Botchan » de Natsume Soseki. Il s'agit d'un simple bonbon préparé en prenant en sandwich des bonbons de riz purs entre des feuilles de bambou séchées. Lorsque vous le mettez en bouche, le parfum rafraîchissant du bambou et la douce douceur du riz fondent lentement. C'est un moment paisible qui rend tellement nostalgique que le temps semble s'arrêter. Il s'agit d'un chef-d'œuvre où l'on peut ressentir la sagesse et la tradition du pays enneigé que la ville portuaire de Naoetsu a continué de protéger.
product_tw:
上越名品“笹雨”
夏目漱石的「少爺」中出現過的歷史悠久的上越特產。這是一種用乾竹葉夾著純米糖製成的簡單甜點。當你把它放進嘴裡時，竹子的清香和米飯的溫和甜味慢慢融化。這是一個寧靜的時刻，讓你感到如此懷舊，時間似乎停止了。這是可以感受到港口城市直江津持續守護的雪國智慧和傳統的傑作。

In the past, this platform was filled with long special trains carrying beachgoers. The sound of a train running along the water's edge still evokes nostalgia in the hearts of travelers, and the gentle sound of the sea helps them forget the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

When you look at the silhouettes of boats lined up at a small fishing port, you want to surrender to the leisurely flow of time.

The vibrancy of the market, where seafood is lined up after being tossed by the rough waves, gives you a sense of the harsh yet rich Hokuriku climate.

product_ja:
海辺の宿「うみてらす名立」の魚介味噌漬け
日本海に沈む夕日が美しい名立の港町。ここで厳選された銀だらや鮭を、地元産の風味豊かな味噌に漬け込んだ逸品です。低温でじっくりと熟成された身は、味噌の甘みと魚の脂が完璧に融合。焼けば焦げた味噌の香ばしさが家中を満たし、白米との無限ループへと誘います。名立の潮風を纏った、旅情あふれる朝食の主役です。
product_en:
Miso-pickled seafood at the seaside inn “Umiterasu Nadachi”
The port town of Nadachi has a beautiful sunset over the Sea of Japan. This is a masterpiece made with carefully selected silver codfish and salmon marinated in locally produced flavorful miso. The meat is slowly aged at a low temperature, and the sweetness of the miso and the fat of the fish are a perfect fusion. Once baked, the aroma of burnt miso fills the house, inviting you into an endless loop with white rice. It is the main character of a breakfast filled with the travel spirit, with a taste of Nadachi's sea breeze.
product_fr:
Fruits de mer marinés au miso à l’auberge balnéaire « Umiterasu Nadachi »
La ville portuaire de Nadachi offre un magnifique coucher de soleil sur la mer du Japon. Il s'agit d'un chef-d'œuvre à base de morue argentée et de saumon soigneusement sélectionnés, marinés dans un miso savoureux produit localement. La viande vieillit lentement à basse température, et la douceur du miso et le gras du poisson forment une fusion parfaite. Une fois cuit, l’arôme du miso brûlé remplit la maison, vous invitant dans une boucle sans fin avec le riz blanc. C'est le personnage principal d'un petit-déjeuner empli de l'esprit du voyage, avec un avant-goût de la brise marine de Nadachi.
product_tw:
海濱旅館「Umiterasu Nadachi」的味增海鮮
港口城市那立能夠欣賞日本海上美麗的日落。這是用嚴選的銀鱈魚和鮭魚用當地生產的美味味噌醃製而成的傑作。肉在低溫下慢慢熟成，味噌的甜味和魚的脂肪完美融合。出爐後，燒焦的味噌香氣充滿整個房子，邀請您與白米飯無限循環。這是一份充滿旅行精神、帶有那立海風味道的早餐的主角。

The appearance of this "Mole Station" makes you feel the tenacity of railway technology and the ruggedness of the journey through the mountains.

product_ja:
能生産 紅ズワイガニ（直送品）
「道の駅 マリンドリーム能生」でも絶大な人気を誇る、能生自慢の紅ズワイガニ。海洋深層水が育んだ身は、驚くほど瑞々しく、口に入れた瞬間に強烈な甘みが弾けます。お取り寄せでは、ボイルしたての鮮度を封じ込めてお届け。カニ味噌の濃厚なコクを身に絡めていただけば、そこはもう能生の漁港。カニ好きを虜にする「海の赤い宝石」です。
product_en:
Noh Production Red Snow Crab (Directly Delivered)
Nou's signature red snow crab is extremely popular at Roadside Station Marine Dream Nou. The meat, grown in deep ocean water, is surprisingly fresh and bursts with intense sweetness the moment you put it in your mouth. When ordered, the freshness of freshly boiled food is sealed and delivered. Once you taste the rich flavor of crab miso, you'll be transported to Nou's fishing port. It is the ``red jewel of the sea'' that captivates crab lovers.
product_fr:
Noh Production Crabe des neiges rouge (livré directement)
Le crabe des neiges rouge emblématique de Nou est extrêmement populaire à Roadside Station Marine Dream Nou. La viande, cultivée dans les eaux profondes de l'océan, est étonnamment fraîche et éclate d'une douceur intense dès que vous la mettez dans votre bouche. Lors de la commande, la fraîcheur des aliments fraîchement bouillis est scellée et livrée. Une fois que vous aurez goûté la riche saveur du miso de crabe, vous serez transporté au port de pêche de Nou. C'est le « joyau rouge de la mer » qui captive les amateurs de crabe.
product_tw:
能劇紅雪蟹（直送）
Nou 的招牌紅雪蟹在 Roadside Station Marine Dream Nou 非常受歡迎。生長在深層海水中的肉質出奇的新鮮，入口即化出濃鬱的甜味。訂購時，新鮮煮食的新鮮度被密封並交付。一旦您品嚐到蟹味噌的濃鬱風味，您就會被帶到諾烏的漁港。它是令螃蟹愛好者著迷的「海洋紅色寶石」。

product_ja:
幻魚（げんぎょ）の一夜干し
かつては「幻の魚」とされた深海魚。見た目からは想像もつかない、驚くほど上品な白身と、プルプルのコラーゲン質が特徴です。軽く炙れば、香ばしい皮目から上質な脂が弾け出し、口の中でとろけるような甘みが広がります。青海の荒波が育んだ、まさに「深海の貴婦人」。地酒「加賀の井」との相性は、語るまでもなく最高です。
product_en:
Dried phantom fish overnight
A deep-sea fish that was once considered a "mythical fish." It is characterized by a surprisingly elegant white flesh and jiggly collagen that you wouldn't expect from its appearance. When lightly grilled, the high-quality fat bursts out from the fragrant skin, creating a melt-in-your-mouth sweetness. A true "lady of the deep sea", nurtured by the rough waves of the blue sea. It goes without saying that it goes perfectly with the local sake "Kaga no I".
product_fr:
Poisson fantôme séché pendant la nuit
Un poisson des grands fonds qui était autrefois considéré comme un « poisson mythique ». Il se caractérise par une chair blanche étonnamment élégante et un collagène tremblant auquel on ne s'attendrait pas de par son apparence. Lorsqu'elle est légèrement grillée, la graisse de haute qualité jaillit de la peau parfumée, créant une douceur fondante en bouche. Une véritable « dame des profondeurs », nourrie par les vagues agitées de la mer bleue. Il va sans dire qu'il s'accorde parfaitement avec le saké local « Kaga no I ».
product_tw:
幻魚乾隔夜
曾經被認為是「神話魚」的深海魚。它的特點是令人驚訝的優雅白色果肉和參差不齊的膠原蛋白，這是你從它的外觀中意想不到的。輕輕一烤，優質脂肪就從香甜的皮中迸發出來，入口即化的甜味。真正的“深海女士”，是在藍色大海的波濤洶湧中孕育出來的。不用說，它與當地的清酒“加賀之我”非常相配。

text_en: Wisdom teeth. It is a sheer cliff where the Northern Alps fall into the Sea of ​​Japan, and is a difficult place in the world that travelers have risked their lives to pass through since ancient times. The old road that crawls along the shore of the waves and the piers of the expressway built high into the sky are truly the result of civil engineering technology. Hearing the roar of the rough waves biting the rocks makes you feel the hardships of the travelers of the past and the awe of nature.

It evokes a sense of desolation at the prefectural border and the countless travelers who have crossed the road, giving us a sense of sadness as if it were the end of a journey.

text_en:
Gono line. This railway, which starts at Higashi-Noshiro, a branch point from the Ou Main Line, and runs through the Tsugaru plains while being washed by the rough waves of the Sea of ​​Japan, is the very embodiment of the phrase ``traveling at the very end.'' This line, which was once called the ``Noshiro Line'' and ``Goshogawara Line,'' was finally connected as a single chain in 1933.As you pass through Hachimori and Iwadate, the blue Sea of ​​Japan stretches out as far as the eye can see on your left, and the steep greenery of the World Heritage Site Shirakami Mountain Range looms on your right, presenting you with the majesty and harshness of nature at the same time.

The path of the Hachiroku (type 8620), which endured salt damage and braved the sea breeze, has now been inherited by a modern tourist train called the Resort Shirakami, but the scent of the sea that wafts through the station buildings of old port towns such as Fukaura and Ajigasawa still retains the same atmosphere of travel. After admiring the strangely shaped rocks of Senjojiki and passing Ajigasawa, the train steers inland.The magnificent peak of Mt. Iwaki, also known as ``Tsugaru Fuji'', dominates the train window, and apple orchards as far as the eye can see greet us. Traveling along this line, which is a condensation of the sea, mountains, and indigenous lifestyle of Tsugaru, reminds us of the ``purity of travel'' that is irreplaceable in this day and age where efficiency is valued.

Higashi-Noshiro Station. Since its opening in 1909, it has continued to support logistics and travelers in northern Akita as a transportation node connecting the Ou Main Line and the Gono Line. It was once a lively hub for lumber transportation, and now it has become a turning point for travellers, with the scenic trip ``Resort Shirakami'' drastically changing its course and venturing into the Sea of ​​Japan.
product_ja:
田県産 プレミアムあきたこまち（能代産）
五能線の旅の始まりは、米どころ秋田の誇りから。能代の肥沃な大地と、白神山地から流れ込む清らかな水が育んだ「あきたこまち」は、炊き上がりの輝きが違います。口に含めば、噛むほどに優しい甘みが広がり、冷めても失われないもっちりとした食感。まずは塩むすびで、その「純粋な旨味」を五感で受け止めてください。
product_en:
Premium Akitakomachi (produced in Noshiro) from Ta Prefecture
Your journey on the Gono Line begins with the pride of Akita, the rice-producing region. ``Akitakomachi'', which was nurtured by the fertile land of Noshiro and the clean water flowing from the Shirakami Mountains, has a different shine when cooked. When you put it in your mouth, the more you chew, the gentle sweetness spreads out, and the chewy texture doesn't fade even when it gets cold. First, try the salt musubi and enjoy its "pure flavor" with all five senses.
product_fr:
Akitacomachi haut de gamme (produit à Noshiro) de la préfecture de Ta
Votre voyage sur la Gono Line commence par la fierté d'Akita, la région productrice de riz. «Akitakomachi», qui a été nourri par les terres fertiles de Noshiro et l'eau propre coulant des montagnes Shirakami, a un éclat différent une fois cuit. Lorsque vous le mettez dans votre bouche, plus vous mâchez, plus la douceur douce se propage et la texture moelleuse ne s'estompe pas même lorsqu'il fait froid. Tout d'abord, essayez le sel musubi et appréciez sa « saveur pure » avec vos cinq sens.
product_tw:
田縣優質秋小町（能代產）
您的五野線之旅始於稻米產地秋田的驕傲。能代的肥沃土地和白神山流淌的潔淨水孕育出來的“秋小町”，煮熟後呈現出不同的光澤。放入口中，越嚼越柔和的甜味擴散開來，即使冷了也不會失去嚼勁。首先，嚐嚐鹽結，用五種感官享受它的「純正味道」。

text_en: Noshiro station. Since its opening in 1909, it has been known as the face of Bokuto Noshiro, located at the mouth of the Yoneshiro River, and is now a symbol of the basketball town. The basketball goal installed on the platform is proof that the railway has carried the local culture and the passion of young people, and is a stylish display that conveys the vibrancy of the city to passengers.
product_ja:
片栗うどん（檜山うどん）
「木都」能代に伝わる、幻の伝統麺。江戸時代から続く製法を守り、手綯い（てない）で作られる麺は、驚くほど細くありながら、絹のような滑らかさと力強いコシを併せ持ちます。喉を通る瞬間の心地よさは、まさに職人技の結晶。能代の歴史が息づく、凛とした味わいをご家庭の食卓でぜひ体感してください。
product_en:
Potato udon (Hiyama udon)
``Bokuto'' A fantastic traditional noodle handed down in Noshiro. The noodles are hand-rolled using a manufacturing method that has been used since the Edo period, and are surprisingly thin, yet have a silky smoothness and a strong chewiness. The feeling of comfort the moment it passes through your throat is truly the result of craftsmanship. Please experience the dignified taste of Noshiro's history at your home dining table.
product_fr:
Udon aux pommes de terre (Hiyama udon)
``Bokuto'' Une fantastique nouille traditionnelle transmise à Noshiro. Les nouilles sont roulées à la main selon une méthode de fabrication utilisée depuis la période Edo. Elles sont étonnamment fines, tout en étant soyeuses et très moelleuses. La sensation de confort au moment où il passe dans votre gorge est véritablement le résultat d’un savoir-faire artisanal. S'il vous plaît, découvrez le goût digne de l'histoire de Noshiro à votre table à manger.
product_tw:
馬鈴薯烏龍麵（檜山烏龍麵）
「Bokuto」 能代流傳下來的美味傳統麵條。麵條採用自江戶時代以來一直沿用的製作方法手工擀製而成，細得驚人，但絲般柔滑，嚼勁十足。穿過喉嚨那一刻的舒適感，確實是工藝的成果。請在您家的餐桌上體驗能代歷史的尊貴味道。

text_en: Mukanoshiro Station. This station, which was built in 1950 at the request of local residents during the post-war reconstruction period, is an important support for the quiet residential area across the Yoneshiro River. For the people who used to look at the city of Noshiro from the other side of the river, the joy of being connected by this railway still blends into the calm atmosphere that surrounds the platform.

Kitanoshiro Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has supported the vast ``Kaze no Matsubara'' and has watched over the lives of the local community while directly receiving the strong winds from the Sea of ​​Japan. If you stand on the unobstructed platform, the sea breeze and the sand will blow, giving you a sense of the harsh yet beautiful coastline journey that is about to begin on the Gono Line.

Torigata station. This unmanned station, which was built in 1960 as the surrounding area was being developed, is a place that feels like a hidden hideout, nestled quietly in the middle of a rural landscape and pine forest as far as the eye can see. You can experience the seasonal expressions of the Noshiro plains most closely, and it shows you how railways are integrated into people's daily lives.

Sawame station. Since its opening in 1922, it has played a simple but important role as the entrance to Happo Town and once as a base for transporting lumber from the mountains. The appearance of the station building, which retains the atmosphere of the Showa era, is a quiet reminder of the bustling days when many lumbermen and peddlers came and went.

Higashihachimori Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has continued to support the lives of this small area of ​​flat land between the mountains and the sea, where fishing villages and farming communities intersect. In spring, the flowers blooming around the platform warmly welcome travelers who have overcome the harsh winter, showing off the benevolent side of the Gono Line.

Yamori Station. Since its opening in 1923, this station has a long history, serving as the gateway to Yamori Fishing Port, which is famous for its sandfish fishing. What was once a lively scene of freight cars laden with freshly caught fish passing by has now been replaced by the quiet sound of waves, reminding us of the weight of the years that railroads have nurtured the local industry.
product_ja:
諸井醸造 秋田塩辛（ハタハタしょっつる）
日本海の波飛沫を浴びる八森。ここには、ハタハタと塩だけで数年かけて熟成させる「しょっつる」の聖地があります。ご紹介するのは、その雫を凝縮したような深み。独特の芳醇な香りが、料理に一滴垂らすだけでプロの味へと昇華させます。八森の漁師たちが守り抜いた、海の発酵芸術。これぞ秋田の魂の味です。
product_en:
Moroi Jozo Akita Salted Fish (Hatahata Shotsuru)
Yamori is bathed in the waves of the Sea of Japan. This is the sacred place for shottsuru, which is aged for several years using only sandfish and salt. What we would like to introduce to you is the depth that condenses those drops. Its unique mellow aroma will give your food a professional taste just by adding a drop of it. The art of sea fermentation has been preserved by the fishermen of Yamori. This is the taste of Akita's soul.
product_fr:
Moroi Jozo Akita Poisson Salé (Hatahata Shotsuru)
Yamori est baignée par les vagues de la mer du Japon. C'est le lieu sacré du shottsuru, qui est vieilli pendant plusieurs années en utilisant uniquement du poisson de sable et du sel. Ce que nous aimerions vous présenter, c'est la profondeur qui condense ces gouttes. Son arôme moelleux unique donnera à vos aliments un goût professionnel simplement en en ajoutant une goutte. L'art de la fermentation marine a été préservé par les pêcheurs de Yamori. C'est le goût de l'âme d'Akita.
product_tw:
諸井丈三秋田鹹魚（旗幡松鶴）
亞森沐浴在日本海的波濤中。這裡是丸鶴的聖地，只使用沙魚和鹽來陳釀數年。我們想向您介紹的是凝結這些水滴的深度。其獨特的醇厚香氣，只需添加一滴即可為您的食物帶來專業的味道。亞森的漁民保留了海洋發酵的藝術。這就是秋田靈魂的味道。

text_en: Takinoma Station. This small station, built in 1963, is located in a spectacular view of the rough waves of the Sea of ​​Japan in front of you and the steep mountains in the background. It is a testament to the railway's ability to overcome the steep terrain that it literally looks like a waterfall, and if you stand on the platform, you can see the dynamic scenery that is the true essence of the Gono Line.

Akita Shirakami Station. It was born in 1997 with the registration of the Shirakami Mountains as a World Natural Heritage Site, and has continued to shine as a new symbol of tourism and regional development. Adjacent to a roadside station, its appearance surrounded by clear water and the scent of greenery symbolizes that the railway has become a bridge in a new era that connects nature conservation and tourism.

Iwadate Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has served as the northernmost station in Akita Prefecture, protecting the border of Aomori Prefecture, and serving as the base of the Iwadate Coast, where the rugged rocky landscape spreads out. It was once a place where steam locomotives took a breather in preparation for crossing the prefectural border pass, and even today, the magnificent setting sun over the Sea of ​​Japan shines beautifully like a lighthouse praying for a safe journey.

Omakoshi Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has served as the first station from Akita to Aomori, welcoming travelers who have crossed the steep mountain road that borders the prefecture. It quietly retains the vestiges of a village that once flourished with forestry, and is the place where you can start a quiet journey that gives you a glimpse of the beauty of the Aomori Prefecture coastline.

Shirakamidake Tozanguchi Station. Since its opening in 1952, it has continued to make its mark as a base for climbers aiming for the highest peak in the World Heritage Site Shirakami Mountains. With the green mountains looming in the background, this station is perfect as a trailhead where you can feel the courage and excitement of going deep into nature, along with the sea breeze.

Matsugami Station. Since its opening in 1923, it is a historic station that has continued to support the lives of the local community through the power of railways in a quiet location a little away from the coastline. It was once a transit point for collecting wood cut from the surrounding mountains, and today, a trace of the industry from that time remains in the serene landscape.

Juniko Station. Since its opening in 1952, it has been attracting tourists from all over the country as the gateway to sightseeing at Juniko Lakes, including the mysterious, sparkling blue Aoike. The benefits of tourism brought by the railway have harmonized with the area's rich nature, and now it has firmly established itself as one of the most popular spots on the Gono Line.
product_ja:
白神山地の天然水（青池ラベル）
世界遺産・白神山地の広大なブナ林が、数百年かけて濾過した奇跡の雫。硬度が非常に低い超軟水で、その口当たりはどこまでも柔らかく、体に染み渡るようです。青池の神秘的な輝きを想起させる透き通った味わいは、お茶や料理の味を最大限に引き出します。自宅にいながら、白神の森の静寂を飲み干すような贅沢を。
product_en:
Natural water of Shirakami Sanchi (Aoike label)
Miraculous drops that have been filtered over hundreds of years by the vast beech forests of the World Heritage Site Shirakami-Sanchi. The water is extremely soft with very low hardness, and its texture is so soft that it seems to soak into your body. Its clear taste, reminiscent of the mysterious glow of Aoike, brings out the maximum flavor of tea and dishes. Enjoy the luxury of immersing yourself in the silence of Shirakami Forest while staying at home.
product_fr:
Eau naturelle de Shirakami Sanchi (label Aoike)
Des gouttes miraculeuses filtrées pendant des centaines d'années par les vastes forêts de hêtres du site du patrimoine mondial Shirakami-Sanchi. L'eau est extrêmement douce avec une très faible dureté et sa texture est si douce qu'elle semble pénétrer dans votre corps. Son goût clair, rappelant l'éclat mystérieux de l'Aoike, fait ressortir au maximum la saveur du thé et des plats. Profitez du luxe de vous immerger dans le silence de la forêt de Shirakami tout en restant chez vous.
product_tw:
白神山地天然水（青池標示）
世界遺產白神山地廣闊的山毛櫸林數百年來過濾出的神奇水滴。水非常軟，硬度很低，質地軟軟的，彷彿要浸入身體裡。其清澈的味道，讓人想起青池的神秘光芒，最大限度地襯托出茶和菜餚的風味。足不出戶即可享受沉浸在白神森林靜謐之中的奢華體驗。

text_en: Mutsu Iwasaki Station. Since its opening in 1920, it has prospered as an intermediate hub on the Gono Line and a key logistics hub with a large fishing port. During its heyday in the Showa era, many people came and went, and the pride of the times when local industry and railways were closely connected can still be seen in the dignified appearance around the station.

Mutsusawabe Station. Since its opening in 1933, it has played a role as a transportation route for small fishing villages and as a vital route for commuting to work and school during the harsh winters. Located on top of a coastal terrace, the vast panoramic view of the Sea of ​​Japan seen from the platform is a hideaway with a spectacular view that will make you feel the real thrill of traveling on the Gono Line.

Wespa Tsubakiyama Station. This new station, built in 1995, is a symbolic presence that breathed new life into local tourism through its integration with resort facilities. Railways have created new value in places where there was nothing before, and along with hot springs where you can watch the sunset, they are proposing a modern style of travel.

Takusaku Station. Since its opening in 1933, the station, also known as the difficult-to-read station name, has quietly watched over the lives of fishermen at the tip of a cape that juts out into the Sea of ​​Japan. Its location, surrounded by rough rocks, is a powerful place that silently tells us how difficult the terrain was to overcome in order to build the railway.

Yokoiso Station. Since its opening in 1955, it has been projecting the scenery of a simple fishing village next to a railway that runs along the edge of the waves of the Sea of ​​Japan. In the past, it was common to see trains running under the tide, and we are reminded of the hard work of those on the ground who supported the train's operation while battling harsh natural conditions.

Fukaura station. Since its opening in 1930, it has held an extremely important position on the Gono Line as the gateway to a port town that has prospered as a port of call for Kitamaebune ships since ancient times. It was once an important railway hub where a locomotive depot was located and locomotives taking on mountainous terrain could catch their breath, and the smell of the salty sea that still wafts in the air today is a testament to the prosperity of the time.
product_ja:
ふかうら雪人参（ジュース・加工品）
雪の下で凍る直前まで耐え忍ぶことで、糖度がフルーツ並みにまで跳ね上がった奇跡の人参。一口飲めば、その「人参とは思えない甘み」に衝撃を受けるはずです。青臭さは微塵もなく、濃厚なコクだけが喉を潤します。厳しい日本海の冬が育んだ大地の甘み。深浦の雪景色と生産者の情熱が詰まった、心温まる逸品です。
product_en:
Fukaura Snow Carrot (juice/processed product)
A miraculous carrot whose sugar content has soared to the level of fruit by enduring it under the snow until just before it freezes. If you take a sip, you'll be shocked by the sweetness that you wouldn't expect from a carrot. There's not a trace of grassy smell, just the rich flavor that moistens your throat. The sweetness of the earth nurtured by the harsh winters of the Sea of ​​Japan. A heart-warming masterpiece packed with the snowy scenery of Fukaura and the passion of the producers.
product_fr:
Carotte des neiges Fukaura (jus/produit transformé)
Une carotte miraculeuse dont la teneur en sucre s'est élevée au niveau d'un fruit en la supportant sous la neige jusqu'au moment où elle gèle. Si vous en prenez une gorgée, vous serez choqué par la douceur que vous n'attendriez pas d'une carotte. Il n’y a aucune trace d’odeur herbacée, juste la riche saveur qui humidifie votre gorge. La douceur de la terre nourrie par les hivers rigoureux de la mer du Japon. Un chef-d'œuvre réconfortant rempli de paysages enneigés de Fukaura et de la passion des producteurs.
product_tw:
深浦雪胡蘿蔔（果汁/加工品）
一種神奇的胡蘿蔔，在雪下直到結冰前，其糖分含量飆升至水果水平。如果你喝一口，你會被胡蘿蔔意想不到的甜味震驚。沒有一絲草香，只有潤喉的濃鬱味道。日本海的嚴冬孕育出大地的甘甜。充滿了深浦的雪景和製作人的熱情的感人傑作。

text_en: Hiroto station. Since its opening in 1955, it has been located on a small flat area beneath a steep cliff, and the impact of the waves can still be felt today. It is a place that makes you feel the weight of history, as this line of railway was once the only hope for connecting to the outside world for the people of the small surrounding villages.

Oirase Station. Since opening in 1933, we have lived close to the mouth of the Oirase River, living in harmony with the rich natural environment where the river and the sea intersect. It was once a logistics hub where timber transport from upstream and railways intersected, and as you stand on the quiet platform, you can hear the sounds of water and remember the history of railways.

Hakogi station. Since its opening in 1933, it has become a sacred place for railway fans, with the wooden station building reflecting the setting sun and being said to be the most beautiful in Japan, as the name suggests. It is a blissful place where you can stand alone on an unobstructed platform and enjoy the ultimate sense of travel while watching the sun set on the horizon.

Kawase Station. Since opening in 1930, we have continued to protect the safety of the area in a rugged area where strong winds blow directly from the Sea of ​​Japan. In this place where the wind literally matches, it is immeasurable how much the lights of the trains, which appear on time even during a winter blizzard, have encouraged the hearts of the residents.

Otose Station. Since its opening in 1930, it has provided travelers with a moment of peace as a base along the vast rocky coastline. The many strange-looking rocks that tower in the vicinity are works of art created by the Sea of ​​Japan over many years, and the railway provides us with the luxury of being able to admire them from the train window.

Senjojiki Station. Since its opening in 1927, it has become famous throughout the country as the entrance to the legendary rocky place where lords once held banquets on 1,000 tatami mats. It used to be a temporary station, but now it is a banquet hall of nature, with the resort Shirakami also stopping there as a highlight with a spectacular view.

Kitakanegasawa Station. Since its opening in 1939, this area, which is home to the largest ginkgo tree in Japan, has functioned as an important relay point for trains passing through each other. It once had a prosperous history as a port of refuge for Kitamaebune ships, and the station has a dignified atmosphere that symbolizes the strength of the railway as it crosses the raging sea.

Mutsu Yanagida Station. Since its opening in 1952, the area has supported a lifestyle where agriculture and fishing intersect, in a place where the sea gradually recedes and the Tsugaru plain begins to feel expansive. There was once a time when the area was looked upon as a distribution point for goods as development progressed in the surrounding area, and today the railway has blended into the peaceful rural landscape.

Mutsu Akaishi Station. Since our opening in 1929, we have enjoyed the clear waters of the Akashi River and the rich bounty of the region along with the sweetfish that swim upstream. Even in the past, despite being exposed to the ravages of nature, such as bridges being damaged by river flooding, the tenacity of railways has been repeatedly restored with an indomitable spirit, and the sound of the rails can still be heard today.

Ajigasawa Station. Since its opening in Taisho 14, it has reigned as the largest base on the Tsugaru West Coast, with a history of flourishing as a port of call for Kitamaebune ships. The style of the station building reflects the pride of the heyday of the railroad, when freight cars laden with seafood departed across the country in the wind blowing from the mountains, bringing great wealth to the city.
product_ja:
鰺ヶ沢名物 焼きイカ（冷凍・真空パック）
駅に降り立った瞬間に鼻をくすぐる、あの香ばしい「イカ焼き通り」の香りを自宅で。日本海の潮風で干されたイカを、絶妙な焼き加減で仕上げた逸品です。噛むほどに溢れ出す旨味と、ぷりっとした弾力。お取り寄せなら、軽く炙るだけであの浜辺の情景が蘇ります。地酒のお供にはもちろん、お子様のおやつにも最適です。
product_en:
Ajigasawa specialty grilled squid (frozen/vacuum packed)
Enjoy the fragrant scent of "Squid Grilled Street" that tickles your nose the moment you step off the station at home. This is a masterpiece made with perfectly grilled squid that has been dried in the sea breeze of the Sea of ​​Japan. The more you bite into it, the flavor overflows and the chewy texture. If you order it, just lightly roasting it will bring back that beach scene. Perfect to accompany local sake, or as a snack for children.
product_fr:
Calmar grillé, spécialité d'Ajigasawa (surgelé/emballé sous vide)
Profitez du parfum parfumé de « Squid Grilled Street » qui vous chatouille le nez dès que vous sortez de la gare chez vous. Il s'agit d'un chef-d'œuvre réalisé avec des calamars parfaitement grillés et séchés dans la brise marine de la mer du Japon. Plus vous mordez dedans, plus la saveur déborde et la texture moelleuse. Si vous le commandez, il suffit de le rôtir légèrement pour ramener cette scène de plage. Parfait pour accompagner le saké local, ou comme collation pour les enfants.
product_tw:
鰺澤特產烤魷魚（冷凍/真空包裝）
在家門口一出站，就能聞到撲鼻而來的「魷魚烤街」的香味。這是用在日本海的海風中乾燥的完美烤魷魚製成的傑作。越咬下去，味道溢出來，口感也有嚼勁。如果你點了它，只需輕輕烘烤一下，就會帶回海灘的景色。非常適合搭配當地清酒，或作為兒童零食。

text_en: Narusawa Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has served as a point of departure for local farmers as they step inland from the coastline. It is a simple station that once carried the hopes of pioneering farmers in the surrounding area, and now continues to quietly watch over the four seasons of Tsugaru amid the quiet passage of time.

Koshimizu Station. Since its opening in 1954, it has been a valuable means of transportation for local residents amidst the unique topography dotted with vast wetlands and swamps. It once helped the modernization of peat mining and agriculture in the surrounding area, and now, with its calm water scenery, it is a place where you can feel the peace that is inherent to local trains.

Mutsu Morita Station. Since its opening in 1923, the station has carved out history in the rich grain belt of the Tsugaru Plain, with a station building that retains the vestiges of Taisho romance. It was once a busy place for shipping rice, and now it is attracting attention as an entrance to the surrounding Jomon ruins, and the railway connects the vitality of this area from ancient times to the present day.

Nakata station. Since its opening in 1955, it has warmly supported local school commuters and people working hard in the middle of vast rice fields. It is a small station filled with happy memories, where the platform was once filled with the laughter of children attending schools in the area, and where the railway carried treasures that would hold the future of the region.

wooden station. Since its opening in 1922, the station has amazed the world with its huge clay figurine, ``Shakochan,'' which is enshrined on the wall of the station building. It once prospered as a center for the development of the surrounding wetlands, and is now the epicenter of Jomon culture, making it a unique hub where the railway invites travelers to delve into the depths of history.

Goshogawara Station. Since its opening in 1912, it has been responsible for the development of the city as a main artery for the gathering of goods from the Tsugaru Plain and as a connection point with the Tsugaru Railway. The hustle and bustle of the days when the excitement of Tachikenputa enveloped the station and freight trains stretched out in all directions continues to be passed down to this day as the powerful heartbeat of the city.
product_ja:
津軽塗（つがるぬり）の箸
「立佞武多」が夜空を焦がす熱き街、五所川原。ここで守られる津軽塗は、数十回の塗り、研ぎ、磨きを繰り返す「馬鹿塗り」とも呼ばれる手仕事の極致です。手にした時のしっくりとくる重み、そして使い込むほどに艶を増す美しい斑模様。日本の食卓を支える「用の美」は、日々の食事を特別な儀式へと変えてくれるはずです。
product_en:
Tsugaru lacquered chopsticks
Goshogawara is a hot town where the night sky is scorched by Tachineputa. The Tsugaru lacquerware preserved here is the ultimate in handiwork, also known as ``baka lacquering,'' which involves applying, sanding, and polishing dozens of times. It has a nice weight to it when you hold it in your hand, and a beautiful mottled pattern that becomes more lustrous the more you use it. The beauty of use that supports the Japanese dining table is sure to transform everyday meals into special rituals.
product_fr:
Baguettes laquées Tsugaru
Goshogawara est une ville chaude où le ciel nocturne est brûlé par Tachineputa. Les laques Tsugaru conservées ici constituent le summum du travail manuel, également connu sous le nom de « laquage baka », qui implique d'appliquer, de poncer et de polir des dizaines de fois. Il a un joli poids lorsque vous le tenez dans votre main et un magnifique motif marbré qui devient plus brillant à mesure que vous l'utilisez. La beauté de l'utilisation qui soutient la table à manger japonaise transformera à coup sûr les repas quotidiens en rituels spéciaux.
product_tw:
津輕漆筷
五所川原是個夜空被立佞燒焦的炎熱小鎮。這裡保存的津輕漆器是手工技藝的巔峰之作，也被稱為“baka漆器”，需要經過數十次的塗抹、打磨和拋光。當你把它拿在手裡時，它的重量很好，並且有美麗的斑駁圖案，隨著你使用它的次數越來越多，它會變得更加有光澤。日本餐桌的使用之美肯定會將日常膳食變成特殊的儀式。

text_en: Mutsu Tsuruta Station. Since its opening in 1919, it has been a popular gateway to the beautiful lake known for Tsurunomai Bridge and the rich rural landscape of Tsugaru. It once had a vibrant history, with station staff working day and night to ship apples and rice, and today it soothes the hearts of visitors with its warm hospitality, named after the crane.
product_ja:
完熟スチューベン（ぶどうジュース）
ニューヨーク生まれ、鶴田育ち。雪国ならではの寒暖差が、驚異的な甘みを生む「スチューベン」は鶴田の宝です。その完熟果実を惜しみなく搾ったジュースは、ハチミツを思わせる濃厚な甘みと、爽やかな酸味が絶妙に調和。グラスに注いだ瞬間に広がる高貴な香りは、まさに「飲む宝石」。津軽の秋を贅沢に味わえます。
product_en:
Ripe Steuben (grape juice)
Born in New York, raised in Tsuruta. ``Steuben'' is a treasure of Tsuruta, where the temperature difference unique to a snowy country produces an amazing sweetness. The juice that is generously squeezed from the ripe fruit has a rich sweetness reminiscent of honey and a refreshing acidity that perfectly harmonizes. The noble aroma that spreads the moment you pour it into the glass is truly a "drinking jewel." You can enjoy autumn in Tsugaru in luxury.
product_fr:
Steuben mûr (jus de raisin)
Né à New York, élevé à Tsuruta. « Steuben » est un trésor de Tsuruta, où la différence de température propre à un pays enneigé produit une douceur étonnante. Le jus généreusement pressé du fruit mûr a une riche douceur rappelant le miel et une acidité rafraîchissante qui s'harmonise parfaitement. L'arôme noble qui se propage dès que vous le versez dans le verre est un véritable « bijou à boire ». Vous pouvez profiter de l’automne à Tsugaru dans le luxe.
product_tw:
成熟的斯託本（葡萄汁）
出生於紐約，在鶴田長大。 「Steuben」是鶴田的瑰寶，雪國特有的溫差產生了驚人的甜味。從成熟的果實中大量榨取的果汁具有讓人想起蜂蜜的濃鬱甜味和完美協調的清爽酸度。倒入杯中的那一刻，高貴的香氣就瀰漫開來，堪稱「飲酒中的寶石」。您可以奢華地享受津輕的秋天。

text_en: Tsurudomari Station. Since its opening in 1912, this historic station has stood quietly in a vast apple orchard, carrying the daily life of the area with its sweet scent. In the past, wooden crates filled with bright red apples were piled up on the platform, marking the proud memory of how the railway spread the rich fruits of this area throughout Japan.

Itayagi Station. Since its opening in 1912, it has been Japan's number one apple-producing village and is an important base on the Gono Line, which has progressed along with the development of the industry. Remnants of the era when dedicated lines ran to apple warehouses and freight trains symbolized the city's affluence can still be seen in the spacious premises and the heavy brick warehouses surrounding it.
product_ja:
完熟りんご100%ジュース（無添加）
「りんごの里」板柳から、添加物を一切使わず、丸ごと搾り上げた本物の味。一口飲めば、まるでリンゴ畑を丸かじりしたような、鮮烈な香りと甘酸っぱさが鼻を抜けます。生産者の「一番美味しいリンゴを届けたい」という執念が、この一滴に。黄金色に輝くジュースは、リンゴ農家だけが知っている「本当の贅沢」そのものです。
product_en:
100% ripe apple juice (no additives)
Authentic taste squeezed whole from the ``Ringo no Sato'' Itayagi tree without any additives. When you take a sip, your nose will be filled with a vivid aroma and sweet and sour taste, just like biting into an apple orchard. The producer's tenacity to ``deliver the most delicious apples'' is reflected in this single drop. The golden juice is a true luxury known only to apple farmers.
product_fr:
100% jus de pomme mûre (sans additifs)
Goût authentique pressé entier de l'arbre Itayagi « Ringo no Sato » sans aucun additif. Lorsque vous en prenez une gorgée, votre nez sera rempli d'un arôme vif et d'un goût aigre-doux, tout comme si vous mordiez dans un verger de pommiers. La ténacité du producteur à « livrer les pommes les plus délicieuses » se reflète dans cette seule goutte. Le jus doré est un véritable luxe connu uniquement des pomiculteurs.
product_tw:
100%熟蘋果汁（無添加物）
正宗的味道是從“Ringo no Sato”板谷樹上直接榨取的，不添加任何添加劑。喝一口，鼻間充滿濃鬱的香氣和酸甜的味道，就像咬進蘋果園一樣。生產者「提供最美味的蘋果」的毅力就體現在這一滴蘋果上。金黃色的果汁是只有蘋果種植者才知道的真正的奢侈品。

text_en: Hayashizaki Station. Since opening in 1930, we have carried the pride of being the birthplace of Tsugaru apples, and have conveyed the charm of the railway that runs through apple orchards. The railroads that once shared the hardships of development now offer travelers the best view of apples, with white flowers in the spring and red fruits in the fall.

Fujisaki station. Since its opening in 1919, the railway has continued to support the vitality of the region in this area, where the world-famous variety Fuji was born. In the past, agricultural products and daily necessities from the surrounding area fed the town through this station, and now the station is perfect for the gentle sunsets that give you the feeling that your journey through the Tsugaru plains is nearing its end.
product_ja:
世界の「ふじ」りんご（特選品）
五能線の旅の終わりに、世界で最も愛されるリンゴ「ふじ」の生誕地・藤崎の誇りを。シャリッとした小気味よい食感の後に溢れ出す、たっぷりの蜜と果汁。太陽を浴びて真っ赤に色づいたその姿は、五能線の旅を象徴するフィナーレの輝きです。産地直送で届く「ふじ」の格別な旨さを、ぜひその舌で確かめてください。
product_en:
Fuji apples from around the world (special selection)
At the end of your journey on the Gono Line, enjoy the pride of Fujisaki, the birthplace of the world's most beloved apple, Fuji. Plenty of honey and fruit juice overflows after the crunchy texture. Its bright red color as it bathes in the sun is the final glow that symbolizes the journey on the Gono Line. Please enjoy the special taste of Fuji, which is delivered directly from the farm.
product_fr:
Pommes Fuji du monde entier (sélection spéciale)
À la fin de votre voyage sur la ligne Gono, profitez de la fierté de Fujisaki, lieu de naissance de la pomme la plus appréciée au monde, Fuji. Beaucoup de miel et de jus de fruits débordent après la texture croquante. Sa couleur rouge vif lorsqu'il baigne au soleil est la lueur finale qui symbolise le voyage sur la ligne Gono. S'il vous plaît, savourez le goût particulier du Fuji, livré directement de la ferme.
product_tw:
世界各地富士苹果（特选）
在五野線旅程的終點，享受藤崎的驕傲，這裡是世界上最受歡迎的蘋果富士的發源地。鬆脆的口感後，大量的蜂蜜和果汁溢出。沐浴在陽光下的鮮紅色是像徵五野線旅程的最後光芒。請品嚐從農場直接送來的富士的特殊味道。

text_en: Kawabe station. Since its opening in 1899, it has served as the glorious end point where the Ou Main Line and the Gono Line meet, completing the memories of countless journeys. The majesty of the days when the platforms were crowded with people transferring trains and the railway connected all the arteries of the region still lives on in the brilliance of the intricately intersecting rails.

Nagaoka Station. The gateway to this city that rose like a phoenix from the ashes of war is a major hub served by the Shinkansen, yet it retains a dignified atmosphere akin to bushido. Stepping onto the platform, the sincere expressions of the people remind us that the spirit of "Kome Hyappu" (One Hundred Bags of Rice) still lives on as the city's foundation.
product_ja:
長岡名物 浪花屋製菓「元祖 柿の種」
今や国民的スナックとなった「柿の種」の発祥は、ここ長岡。大正時代、ひょんなことから生まれた歪な形が、独特の「カリッ」という快音を生みました。お取り寄せなら、昔ながらの美しい「缶入り」を。唐辛子のピリッとした刺激と、もち米の香ばしさが織りなすリズムは、一度食べ始めれば止められません。長岡が誇る、永遠の定番です。
product_en:
Nagaoka specialty Naniwaya confectionery “Original Kaki no Tane”
The origin of ``Kaki no Tane'', which has now become a national snack, is here in Nagaoka. During the Taisho era, the distorted shape that was created by chance gave rise to a unique "crispy" sound. If you would like to order it, you can order it in a beautiful old-fashioned can. Once you start eating, you won't be able to stop eating the rhythm of the tangy chili pepper and the aroma of sticky rice. It is an eternal classic that Nagaoka is proud of.
product_fr:
Spécialité Nagaoka Confiserie Naniwaya « Original Kaki no Tane »
L'origine du « Kaki no Tane », devenu aujourd'hui un snack national, se trouve ici à Nagaoka. Durant l'ère Taisho, la forme déformée créée par hasard donnait naissance à un son « croustillant » unique. Si vous souhaitez le commander, vous pouvez le commander dans une belle canette à l'ancienne. Une fois que vous aurez commencé à manger, vous ne pourrez plus vous arrêter de manger au rythme du piment piquant et de l'arôme du riz gluant. C'est un classique éternel dont Nagaoka est fier.
product_tw:
長岡特產浪速屋點心“原始柿種”
現在已成為國民小吃的「柿種」的起源就在長岡。大正時代，偶然創造出的扭曲形狀產生了獨特的「脆」聲。如果您想訂購，可以將其裝在漂亮的老式罐子裡訂購。一旦開始吃，就無法停止吃的節奏，撲鼻的辣椒和糯米的香味。這是長岡引以為傲的永恆經典。

text_en: Yamamoto Isoroku Memorial Museum. Standing on the site of the birthplace of the great admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, this sanctuary conveys the struggles and convictions of a man who lived through the turbulent Showa era. Touching each relic and letter, the cry of a passionate soul who sought peace but could not resist fate pierces the traveler's heart.

Kita-Nagaoka Station. Once lined with oil refineries and factory chimneys where the fires of industry burned red, this area still holds an air of artisan-like fortitude. The texture of the brick buildings and old walls seen from the window quietly narrates the footsteps of the nameless workers who supported Japan's modernization.

Oshiki Station. Sitting alone in the middle of vast farmland, this station offers a luxurious space to purely enjoy the expanse of the Echigo Plain. The blue of the unobstructed sky and the sea of rice changing colors with the seasons are essential spices for the "soul-cleansing" experience of a railway journey.

Mitsuke Station. The entrance to the city once famous for "Mitsuke Knit" carries a hint of elegance mixed with the scent of calm daily life. Walking the streets after disembarking, one might hallucinate the sound of clacking looms, feeling the pride of an era when handiwork shaped the city.
product_ja:
見附ニット 日本製マフラー（MITSUKE KNIT）
「繊維の街」見附。ここで作られるニットは、日本トップクラスの技術力が生み出す、極上の肌触りが特徴です。カシミヤのような柔らかさと、確かな保温性。そして何より、丁寧に編み込まれた生地には、雪国の手仕事ならではの温もりが宿っています。冬の信越線をゆく旅人を温めるような、優しさに満ちた逸品です。
product_en:
Mitsuke Knit Japanese muffler (MITSUKE KNIT)
Mitsuke, the “textile town”. The knits made here are characterized by their exquisite texture, produced by Japan's top-class technology. Soft like cashmere and reliable heat retention. Above all, the carefully woven fabric has a warmth that can only be achieved by handiwork in a snowy country. This is a masterpiece full of kindness that will warm travelers traveling on the Shinetsu Line in winter.
product_fr:
Silencieux japonais Mitsuke Knit (MITSUKE KNIT)
Mitsuke, la « ville textile ». Les tricots fabriqués ici se caractérisent par leur texture exquise, produite par la technologie japonaise de pointe. Doux comme du cachemire et rétention de chaleur fiable. Surtout, le tissu soigneusement tissé dégage une chaleur qui ne peut être obtenue que par le travail manuel dans un pays enneigé. Voilà un chef-d'œuvre plein de bienveillance qui réchauffera les voyageurs voyageant sur la ligne Shinetsu en hiver.
product_tw:
Mitsuke Knit 日本圍巾 (MITSUKE KNIT)
見附，「紡織之鄉」。這裡生產的針織品的特點是質地細膩，採用日本頂級技術生產。如羊絨般柔軟，保暖性可靠。最重要的是，精心編織的布料具有隻有在雪國手工製作才能實現的溫暖。這是一部溫暖冬季信越線旅客的充滿善意的傑作。

name_ja: みつけイングリッシュガーデン
text_en: Mitsuke English Garden. This authentic English-style garden rooted in the soil of Echigo is a place of relaxation where seasonal flowers delight the eyes. Walking along the brick paths enveloped in the scent of roses provides an elegant, exotic moment that makes one forget, for a second, that they are in Niigata.

Obu Station. True to its beautiful name (meaning "belt weaving"), time flows quietly around this station, where old settlements exist in close proximity to the rails. Sitting on a platform bench, the vibration of distant trains transmitted through the earth makes one realize that the railway is truly part of this land.

Tokoji Station. As the name suggests, this area holds a sense of peace, as if the light of faith continues to burn quietly amidst the rural landscape. Watching the rails turn crimson at dusk along with the sound of a distant temple bell brings a mix of loneliness and fulfillment as the journey nears its end.

Sanjo Station. The central station of Sanjo, a city world-renowned for its hardware, has a unique atmosphere where the sound of hard iron meets the passion of the people who create it. Outside the station, old houses where craftsmen once walked continue the legacy, reflecting the rigor and pride of tradition.

Sanjo Kaji Dojo. This workshop, where one can see sparks flying from craftsmen's skills, is a living museum conveying the manufacturing process of Japanese nails and cutlery. Experiencing the weight of the hammer and seeing iron change shape reaffirms that the origin of Japanese manufacturing lies in this land.

Higashi-Sanjo Station. Always bustling as a connection point with the Yahiko Line, this station is filled with the excitement of a railway junction where flows of people intersect. The sight of diverse train cars sliding into the platforms is a powerful scene proving that railways are the lifeblood of this nation.
product_ja:
藤次郎（TOJIRO） オールステンレス三徳包丁
世界に誇る「金物のまち」三条。多くの料理人が全幅の信頼を寄せる「藤次郎」の包丁は、圧倒的な切れ味と美しさが自慢です。継ぎ目のないオールステンレスのボディは衛生的で、手にしっくりと馴染みます。食材を切るたびに、三条の鍛冶職人たちの魂が伝わってくるような、一生モノの「道具」の恵みをお手元に。
product_en:
TOJIRO All stainless steel Santoku knife
Sanjo is a world-renowned ``hardware town.'' Fujijiro knives, trusted by many chefs, are known for their overwhelming sharpness and beauty. The seamless all-stainless steel body is hygienic and fits comfortably in your hand. Every time you cut ingredients, you can feel the soul of Sanjo's blacksmiths, and you will have the gift of a tool that will last a lifetime.
product_fr:
TOJIRO Couteau Santoku tout inox
Sanjo est une « ville de quincaillerie » de renommée mondiale. Les couteaux Fujijiro, auxquels font confiance de nombreux chefs, sont connus pour leur tranchant et leur beauté extraordinaires. Le corps sans couture entièrement en acier inoxydable est hygiénique et tient confortablement dans votre main. Chaque fois que vous coupez des ingrédients, vous ressentez l'âme des forgerons de Sanjo et vous recevrez en cadeau un outil qui durera toute une vie.
product_tw:
TOJIRO 全不銹鋼三德刀
三條是世界著名的「五金之鄉」。藤二郎刀具以其無與倫比的鋒利和美觀而受到許多廚師的信賴。無縫全不銹鋼機身衛生且握在手中舒適。每次切割食材時，你都能感受到三條鐵匠的靈魂，你將獲得一件可以受用一生的工具的禮物。

text_en: Honai Station. Known since ancient times as a town of landscaping, the area around this station is filled with beautifully maintained greenery, making the "entire town look like a garden." The magnificent pine branches and stone arrangements passing by the window are the crystallization of the aesthetic sense nurtured over many years.

Kamo Station. The gateway to this town, praised as the "Little Kyoto of Hokuetsu," possesses an elegant dignity that invites travelers to historic shrines and old townscapes. Walking through the "Gangi" arcades, the scent of traditional paulownia chests makes one feel time slowing down.
product_ja:
新潟加茂産 西洋梨 ル レクチエ（ジュース・加工品）
「越後の小京都」加茂。ここで育つ「ル レクチエ」は、西洋梨の貴婦人と称される至宝です。お取り寄せで人気のジュースやコンポートは、そのとろけるような果肉感と、芳醇すぎる香りを完璧に封じ込めています。一口含めば、加茂の豊かな土壌が育んだ上品な甘みが鼻に抜け、優雅な気分に浸れること間違いなしです。
product_en:
Niigata Kamo pear Le Lectier (juice/processed products)
Kamo, “Little Kyoto of Echigo”. “Le Lectier” grown here is a treasure known as the Lady of Pear. Our juices and compotes, which are popular on order, perfectly contain their melt-in-the-mouth texture and rich aroma. When you take a sip, the elegant sweetness of Kamo's rich soil fills your nose, and you are sure to be immersed in an elegant mood.
product_fr:
Poire Niigata Kamo Le Lectier (jus/produits transformés)
Kamo, « Petit Kyoto d'Echigo ». Le Lectier cultivé ici est un trésor connu sous le nom de Dame de Poire. Nos jus et compotes, appréciés sur commande, contiennent parfaitement leur texture fondante et leur arôme riche. Lorsque vous prenez une gorgée, la douceur élégante du riche sol de Kamo remplit votre nez et vous êtes assuré d'être plongé dans une ambiance élégante.
product_tw:
新潟加茂梨Le Lectier（果汁/加工品）
加茂，有「越後小京都」之稱。這裡種植的“Le Lectier”是被稱為“梨女士”的珍寶。我們的果汁和蜜餞非常受歡迎，完美地保留了入口即化的口感和濃鬱的香氣。當你喝一口時，加茂肥沃土壤的優雅甜味充滿鼻腔，你一定會沉浸在優雅的心情中。

text_en: Kamoyama Park. Spreading behind Kamo Shrine, this park is a symbol of Kamo where snow camellias in spring and autumn leaves color the mountain, merging nature and faith. Climbing the steep stone steps to overlook the town from the observatory, the peace of this town embraced by water and greenery soaks deep into the traveler's heart.

Honai Park. A symbol of the Honai district in Sanjo City, which has long been renowned nationwide as a "Village of Landscaping," this is a sanctuary where the art of greenery breathes. Within its vast grounds, magnificent trees and bonsai, painstakingly cultivated by master gardeners, are displayed in abundance, and the tropical greenhouse—which makes one forget the harsh northern winters—gently envelops the traveler. Stepping inside, one finds "living sculptures" created through long years of dialogue between nature and humanity, transcending the typical definition of a park and reaffirming the profound depth of Sanjo's artisan spirit.

Kawai Tsugunosuke Memorial Hall. This is the site where the soul of Kawai Tsugunosuke remains—the visionary leader of the Nagaoka Clan and a tragic chief retainer who navigated the turbulent end of the Edo period with a spirit of "independence and self-respect." Inside the hall, built on his former residence, his dreams for a modern nation and the agonizing decisions he made to protect his beloved Nagaoka from the flames of war are etched into every artifact and letter. His resolve, brandishing a Gatling gun and declaring armed neutrality without retreating an inch against great powers, continues to be told as a point of pride for Nagaoka's citizens. Just gazing at the exhibits makes one feel the hot pulse of a man who defied his era and remained true to his convictions resonating within the silence.

Hanyuda Station. As the rails weave along the mountain's edge towards the entrance of the vast Echigo Plain, this place breathes the essence of a nostalgic rural landscape. The breeze sweeping across the platform carries the scent of seasonal wildflowers, gently guarding the silence of the journey.

Tagami Station. Located at the foot of Mt. Gomado, where the sound of wind rustling through bamboo groves can be heard, this station is a center of relaxation embraced by nature. Stepping toward the mountains, the presence of famous hot springs that have healed minds and bodies for ages eases the traveler's tension.

Tagami Gomado Onsen. Surrounded by the lush greenery of Mt. Gomado, this spa possesses a serene beauty fitting for a hidden spring of Echigo. Soaking in the bath while catching the faint sound of the Shinetsu Line in the distance, the sunset becomes the finest feast to cure the weariness of travel.

Yashiroda Station. Once bustling with oil extraction and industrial fires, the strong will of the pioneers still melts into the landscape here. The gentle hills around the station quietly narrate the memories of the rails that survived the turbulent waves of modernization to the next generation.

Niigata Prefectural Botanical Garden. This massive greenhouse, condensing the Earth's breath from tropical forests to Echigo's hills, sits on the ground like a "Green Spaceship." The vivid flowers that make one forget the seasons and the water lilies adorning the ponds add a brilliant touch to the rail journey.
name_fr: Jardin botanique de la préfecture de Niigata

text_en: Furutake Station. Bearing a name reflecting the traces of history passed down since the ancient Manyo era, this place retains a simple beauty that even ancient travelers must have paused to admire. The golden ears of rice viewed from the platform inspire pride in this "Land of Rice," the spiritual home of the Japanese people.

Niitsu Station. The heart of the "Railway Town," where the Shinetsu, Banetsu West, and Uetsu Main lines cross, is a hallowed ground filled with the pride and energy of the rails. The resonance of various train cars reflects the passionate heartbeat of the railwaymen who have supported Japan's main arteries.
product_ja:
越後銘酒 越の寒中梅（こしのかんちゅうばい）
かつての「鉄道の要衝」新津。ここからお届けするのは、新潟が誇る淡麗辛口の真髄です。厳選された酒造好適米と、阿賀野川の伏流水で醸されたこの酒は、喉を通る瞬間のキレが抜群。それでいて、後味には米の柔らかな旨味がそっと残ります。新津の鉄道の歴史に乾杯したくなるような、凛とした風格を持つ一本です。
product_en:
Echigo famous sake Koshi no Kanchubai
Niitsu was once an important railway hub. What we deliver here is the essence of Niigata's proud Tanrei Dry. Brewed with carefully selected rice suitable for sake brewing and underground water from the Agano River, this sake has an outstanding sharpness the moment it passes through your throat. However, the soft flavor of rice remains in the aftertaste. This is a dignified piece that will make you want to toast to Niitsu's railway history.
product_fr:
Le célèbre saké d'Echigo Koshi no Kanchubai
Niitsu était autrefois une plaque tournante ferroviaire importante. Ce que nous livrons ici est l'essence du fier Tanrei Dry de Niigata. Brassé avec du riz soigneusement sélectionné adapté au brassage du saké et de l'eau souterraine de la rivière Agano, ce saké possède un piquant exceptionnel dès son passage dans la gorge. Cependant, la douce saveur du riz demeure dans l’arrière-goût. C'est une pièce digne qui vous donnera envie de porter un toast à l'histoire ferroviaire de Niitsu.
product_tw:
越後名酒越乾中梅
新津曾經是重要的鐵路樞紐。我們在這裡提供的是新潟引以為傲的 Tanrei Dry 的精髓。採用嚴選的適合釀酒的米和阿賀野川的地下水釀造而成，入口即刻的口感十分出色。然而，回味中仍保留著米飯的柔軟味道。這是一件莊重的作品，會讓您想為新津的鐵路歷史乾杯。

text_en: Niitsu Railway Museum. This hall, where steam locomotives and famous train cars spend their retirement, is a time capsule conveying the dreams and passion of the golden age of rail. Touching the heavy bodies and sitting in the driver's seat, the whistle echoes through time, making one feel the eternal history of the rails.

Satsukino Station. Away from the bustle of Niitsu, this station with its expanding new townscape symbolizes that the railway always walks alongside the new era. Even the footsteps of commuters morning and evening are engraved on the tracks as a refreshing rhythm announcing the town's development.

Ogikawa Station. Close to the majestic flow of the Agano River, this land blessed by water preserves a tradition of rich agricultural culture. The rows of pine trees acting as windbreaks seen from the window quietly tell of the wisdom and effort of predecessors who faced harsh nature.

Kameda Station. Once renowned nationwide for its sturdy "Kameda-jima" textiles, this town possesses a unique atmosphere where artisan spirit and merchant energy mix. Upon disembarking, traces of old moats and traditional houses reveal the prosperity of its time as a major logistics hub.

Kameda-jima Textile Village. The indigo-dyed fabric, strong against mud and loved for farm work, is a "Blue Jewel" symbolizing the indomitable spirit of the Echigo people. Listening to the sound of the looms still carefully preserved, it teaches the value of truly precious things in a modern world where handwork is fading.

Echigo-Ishiyama Station. Approaching the final stop of Niigata, this station transitioning into an urban face is filled with the anticipation of journeys ending and beginning. Adjacent to the rail yard, this place shows that the serious gaze of the backstage crew supports the foundation of railway safety.

Niigata Station. The terminus of the long journey and the reigning throne of the Sea of Japan side, this grand terminal is where the dreams of Echigo converge. Stepping onto the modern elevated platform, one feels gratitude for the rails that carried them here, along with the excitement of being drawn toward a new journey.
product_ja:
新潟名物 笹だんご（田中屋本店）
上越新幹線の終着駅、新潟。旅の締めくくりに欠かせないのが、爽やかな笹の香りに包まれた「笹だんご」です。信濃川のほとりで育ったヨモギを贅沢に練り込んだお餅は、驚くほど色濃く、香りが鮮烈。中には上品な甘さの粒あんがぎっしり詰まっています。笹を剥く瞬間の高揚感は、新潟の春と歴史を丸ごと味わうような、贅沢な体験です。
product_en:
Niigata specialty Sasa Dango (Tanakaya main store)
Niigata is the terminal station of the Joetsu Shinkansen. A must-have at the end of your trip is ``Sasa Dango,'' which is filled with the refreshing scent of bamboo. The rice cake is made with luxurious mugwort grown on the banks of the Shinano River, and has a surprisingly deep color and a strong aroma. Inside is packed with elegant sweet bean paste. The exhilarating feeling you get when you peel the bamboo leaves is a luxurious experience that lets you fully experience Niigata's spring and history.
product_fr:
Spécialité Niigata Sasa Dango (magasin principal de Tanakaya)
Niigata est la gare terminale du Joetsu Shinkansen. Un incontournable à la fin de votre voyage est « Sasa Dango », qui regorge du parfum rafraîchissant du bambou. Le gâteau de riz est fait avec de l'armoise luxueuse cultivée sur les rives de la rivière Shinano et a une couleur étonnamment profonde et un arôme puissant. L’intérieur est rempli d’une élégante pâte de haricots sucrés. La sensation exaltante que vous ressentez lorsque vous épluchez les feuilles de bambou est une expérience luxueuse qui vous permet de vivre pleinement le printemps et l'histoire de Niigata.
product_tw:
新潟特產Sasa團子（田中屋總店）
新潟是上越新幹線的終點站。旅行結束時一定要嚐嚐充滿竹子清香的「竹丸子」。年糕是用信濃川沿岸生長的名貴艾草製成的，顏色深得出奇，香氣濃鬱。裡面充滿了優雅的甜豆沙。剝開竹葉時的爽快感是一種奢華的體驗，可以讓您充分體驗新潟的春天和歷史。

text_en: Naoetsu. This place was once the junction of the main railway arteries on the Sea of ​​Japan side, where the Shinetsu Main Line and the Hokuriku Main Line intersected. The night express ``Noto'' and the limited express ``Shiratori'' from Osaka constantly departed from Ueno, and many travelers would repeatedly change trains here to head to the snowy areas of Shinshu and Echigo, or to Toyama and Kanazawa. Although the hustle and bustle of that time is long gone, the scent of the sea and the somewhat melancholy appearance that is unique to a port town are still alive and well. With the opening of the Hokuriku Shinkansen, it became a third sector railway, but in front of the station are lined up merchant houses that still retain the atmosphere of the past, reminding us of the bustle of the past. You can feel that the history nurtured by the rough waves of the Sea of ​​Japan and the lives of the people connected by the railway are deeply engraved in this land.
product_ja:
直江津名産 鱈（たら）の親子漬け
信越本線の終着、直江津。ここで古くから愛されるのが、鱈の身と卵を甘酸っぱい特製酢で漬け込んだ「親子漬け」です。プチプチと弾ける卵の食感と、しっとりとした鱈の身が奏でるハーモニー。箸が止まらなくなるその味わいは、まさに酒泥棒、ご飯泥棒。日本海の冬の厳しさと、港町の温かな知恵が詰まった逸品です。
product_en:
Naoetsu specialty pickled cod with parent and child
Naoetsu is the last stop on the Shinetsu Main Line. A dish that has been loved here for a long time is ``Oyakozuke'', which is made by pickling cod meat and eggs in a special sweet and sour vinegar. A harmony between the popping texture of the egg and the moist cod meat. The taste that you won't be able to stop using your chopsticks is like a sake thief or a rice thief. This is a masterpiece that combines the harshness of winter on the Sea of ​​Japan with the warm wisdom of a port town.
product_fr:
Morue marinée spécialité Naoetsu avec parent et enfant
Naoetsu est le dernier arrêt de la ligne principale Shinetsu. Un plat apprécié ici depuis longtemps est le « Oyakozuke », qui est préparé en faisant mariner de la viande de morue et des œufs dans un vinaigre aigre-doux spécial. Une harmonie entre la texture pétillante de l'œuf et la chair moelleuse du cabillaud. Le goût que vous ne pourrez pas arrêter d'utiliser vos baguettes est celui d'un voleur de saké ou d'un voleur de riz. Il s’agit d’un chef-d’œuvre qui allie la rigueur de l’hiver sur la mer du Japon à la sagesse chaleureuse d’une ville portuaire.
product_tw:
直江津特產醃鱈魚與父母和孩子一起
直江津是信越本線的終點站。這裡長期以來一直深受人們喜愛的菜餚是“親子漬”，它是用特製的糖醋醋醃製鱈魚肉和雞蛋製成的。雞蛋的爆裂口感和濕潤的鱈魚肉之間的和諧。那種讓人停不下筷子的味道，就像是酒賊、飯賊一樣。這是一部將日本海上的嚴冬與港口小鎮的溫暖智慧融為一體的傑作。

text_en: Kuroi. It is a station where you can feel the pulse of industry, with vast freight yards spreading out on both sides and the roar of heavy diesel locomotives shaking the air. In the past, there were many side tracks that led to Naoetsu Port, and the pride that supported the industrial development of this area still seems to reside in the rusted ends of the rails. The sight of a long freight train quietly waiting to depart while being blown by the humid sea breeze is a reminder of the strength of the days when railways were the main means of logistics.

Saigata. As the turning point where the Hokuetsu Express separates from the Shinetsu Main Line, it is a place that retains strong memories of the former limited express ``Hakutaka.'' It used to be a busy station where express trains stopped and people could transfer to Joetsu, but now it has the feel of a quiet, unmanned station. Even so, the occasional wind pressure from the passing trains seems to show off that this area is still an important railway hub, and allows you to experience the dynamism of the railway firsthand.

Dosoko Beach. Once you pass through the windbreak pine trees, you can see the wild Sea of ​​Japan, making it a truly quiet seaside station. The sound of the word ``dosoko'', which is the origin of the station's name, hints at the tenacious lifestyle of the people who have struggled with the soil and lived in harmony with the sea in this sand dune area since ancient times. When you look out the window of a train running along the shore of the ocean and see the horizon dyed by the setting sun, it gives you a feeling of blissful solitude, as if you have arrived at the end of a journey.

Lagoon town. Blessed with waterside scenery such as Unoshima, large ponds, and small ponds, it is a place full of emotion, with literary figures and artists once admiring its scenery. The scent of hot water wafting from the nearby Unohama Onsen gently relieves the fatigue of your travels, and the sight of migratory birds flying by the lake quietly announces the changing seasons. The remains of an old post town and the calm atmosphere created by nature will teach you the depth of Echigo that you would never be able to experience on a quick trip.

Shimohama. It is a place with a deep atmosphere of ``living with the sea'', where you can literally see the flowers of the waves dancing right next to the railroad tracks. In the past, there was a history of battles with landslides and coastal erosion in this area, but now the scenery of a peaceful fishing village has spread out. During stormy winter weather, the waves crashing so powerfully that they almost reach the platforms, giving us a keen sense of the harsh nature of Hokuriku and the resilience of the railways that have overcome it.

Kakizaki. It flourished as a post town on the Hokkoku Kaido Road, and has been a key transportation hub since ancient times, watching over the comings and goings of people. During the Showa era, limited express trains and express trains would slide into its stately platform, and there was a unique vibrancy that mingled with the rich crops of Echigo, the rice-producing region, and the scent of the ocean. Today, the landscape is tranquil, but as you walk through the giant ginkgo trees of Jozenji and the historic streets, you can still feel the vestiges of the wealth and culture that the Kitamaebune brought.
product_ja:
柿崎産 コシヒカリ「米山（よねやま）の恵み」
名峰・米山から流れ出すミネラル豊富な水と、日本海から吹き込む潮風。この絶妙な環境が、お米の甘みを極限まで引き出します。柿崎のコシヒカリは、一粒一粒がどっしりと力強く、噛むほどに濃密な米の香りが鼻を抜けます。おかずは何も要らない。ただ炊きたての真っ白なご飯を頬張る。それが一番の贅沢だと気づかせてくれるお米です。
product_en:
Koshihikari from Kakizaki “Blessings of Yoneyama”
Mineral-rich water flowing from the famous mountain, Mt. Yoneyama, and sea breeze blowing in from the Sea of Japan. This exquisite environment brings out the sweetness of the rice to the utmost. Each grain of Kakizaki's Koshihikari rice is strong and strong, and the more you chew, the rich aroma of rice will hit your nose. No side dishes needed. Just stuff your mouth with freshly cooked pure white rice. This is rice that makes you realize that it is the most luxurious thing.
product_fr:
Koshihikari de Kakizaki « Bénédictions de Yoneyama »
Eau riche en minéraux provenant de la célèbre montagne, le mont Yoneyama, et brise marine soufflant de la mer du Japon. Cet environnement exquis fait ressortir au maximum la douceur du riz. Chaque grain de riz Koshihikari de Kakizaki est fort et fort, et plus vous mâchez, le riche arôme du riz vous frappera le nez. Aucun plat d'accompagnement n'est nécessaire. Farcissez simplement votre bouche avec du riz blanc pur fraîchement cuit. C'est du riz qui vous fait comprendre que c'est la chose la plus luxueuse.
product_tw:
柿崎越光《米山的祝福》
從名山米山流出的富含礦物質的水和從日本海吹來的海風。這種優美的環境將米飯的甜味發揮到了極致。柿崎的越光米每一粒都粒粒飽滿，越嚼越香，濃鬱的米香撲鼻而來。不需要配菜。只要將剛煮熟的純白米飯塞進嘴裡即可。這是讓你意識到它是最奢侈的東西的米飯。

text_en: Yoneyama. It is one of the most spectacular views, with the sacred Mt. This difficult passage, once crossed by steam locomotives, has now been transformed into a blissful train window overlooking the blue ocean below with the quiet sound of the motor. The way Gojo Falls pours into the sea and the many strangely shaped rocks washed by the rough waves make you feel the beauty of nature and the strength of the railway that weaves through it.

Kasashima. It is a truly modest fishing village station, nestled close to a small cove. Even today, the platform is filled with the kind of ethereal silence that was loved by the writers of the Showa era, and if you listen carefully, all you can hear is the sound of the waves and the cries of seagulls. This miniature garden-like landscape that spreads out between tunnels for a moment gives a sense of peace to the journey, and makes you feel the joy of encountering the unchanging, original landscape of Japan.

Aomi River. It is known as the station closest to the sea in Japan, and the waves crashing right below the platform make it look like a stage floating on the sea. Overcoming the hardships of being damaged by the Chuetsu-oki Earthquake, the red overpass was rebuilt strongly and has now become a landmark symbolizing the region's recovery and love for the railway. The moment the sun sets on the horizon, painting the railroad tracks a golden color, the sound of the waves crashing against the ocean, and the deep emotion of the intersection of the end and the beginning of a journey.

Whale wave. This station on the Shin-etsu Main Line is a place that is like a treasure chest of travellers, with a magnificent view of the Sea of ​​Japan behind it. The origin of the place's name comes from the legend that it was once visited by whales, or from the appearance of violent waves crashing against it, which speaks to the harshness and richness of the natural environment of this area. As the train rumbles along the coastline lined with sheer cliffs, the sight of the sunset spreading out through the train window is indescribably beautiful, and many travelers have been captivated by this scenery since the Showa era. Even today, the scene remains unchanged and continues to leave a deep impression on visitors. Kujiranami Beach, which is especially crowded during the summer swimming season, remains as charming as ever. This station is not just a passing point, but an important presence that creates memorable scenery.
