**Kashiwazaki. ** This port town facing the Sea of ​​Japan in the snowy country of Echigo was once the ``best oil base in the East,'' and still quietly tells us of its prosperity. During the high economic growth period of the Showa era, from the windows of the Shinetsu Main Line, now the Echigo Tokimeki Railway, which ran through this area, you could see the sea breeze mixed with the smell of oil and the vibrant activities of the people. The station has a long history, and since its opening in the Meiji era, it has been a lifeline that has continued to support local logistics and people's lives. Although the Sea of ​​Japan looks rough in the winter, it is still bustling with people during festivals, and its warmth is reminiscent of a bygone era.

**Kashiwazaki. ** This area, where the Echigo Line traverses the Echigo Plain and flows into the Sea of ​​Japan, was once known as the ``best oil city in the East'' and literally supported Japan's energy. As you walk through the station premises, which still retains a strong Showa era atmosphere, you will see scenes everywhere that remind you of the prosperity of the time. The flavor of Uonuma-produced Koshihikari, which is served on ekiben, makes you feel the blessings unique to this region. Recently, new efforts have been made to revitalize the area, creating a unique atmosphere where the good old and the new coexist.

**Kashiwazaki. ** As a station on the Echigo Tokimeki Railway that runs along the Sea of ​​Japan, this port town's history is a story of its history with railways. During the Showa era, this place prospered due to the oil industry and was visited by many people. The appearance of the station still retains a faint but unmistakable vestige of those days. If you walk through the shopping streets around the station, you'll find sweets made with the local specialty ``hakka'' and dishes made with seafood from the Sea of ​​Japan, making your trip even more enjoyable.
product_ja:
柏崎名物 鯛茶漬けセット
日本海に面した柏崎。ここで愛される「鯛茶漬け」は、ご当地グルメの最高峰です。お取り寄せなら、新鮮な鯛の身と、出汁、そして薬味がセットに。熱々の出汁を注いだ瞬間に、鯛の身が白く花開き、香ばしい香りが立ち上がります。柏崎の青い海を眺めながらいただくような、贅沢で滋味深い一杯をぜひご自宅で。
product_en:
Kashiwazaki specialty sea bream chazuke set
Kashiwazaki faces the Sea of Japan. The ``Tai Chazuke'' that is loved here is the pinnacle of local gourmet food. If you order, the set includes fresh sea bream meat, soup stock, and condiments. The moment you pour the piping hot soup stock, the sea bream's flesh turns white and blooms, releasing a fragrant aroma. Enjoy a luxurious and nutritious cup at home while looking out at the blue sea of ​​Kashiwazaki.
product_fr:
Set de chazuke à la daurade, spécialité Kashiwazaki
Kashiwazaki fait face à la mer du Japon. Le « Tai Chazuke » apprécié ici est le summum de la gastronomie locale. Si vous commandez, l'ensemble comprend de la viande de daurade fraîche, du bouillon de soupe et des condiments. Dès que vous versez le bouillon bien chaud, la chair de la daurade blanchit et s'épanouit, libérant un arôme parfumé. Savourez une tasse luxueuse et nutritive à la maison tout en regardant la mer bleue de Kashiwazaki.
product_tw:
柏崎特產鯛魚茶泡飯套餐
柏崎面向日本海。這裡深受人們喜愛的「太茶泡飯」是當地美食的巔峰之作。如果點餐的話，套餐還包括新鮮的鯛魚肉、湯料和調味品。剛倒入滾燙的湯汁，鯛魚的肉就變白綻放，散發出陣陣芳香。在家一邊眺望柏崎蔚藍的大海，一邊享用一杯奢華營養的飲品。

text_en: Thorn eyes. This route, which has continued since the Meiji era, once supported the local economy and was a lifeline closely connected to people's lives. In particular, I hear that this ○○ station once prospered as a cluster of △△ industries, and many freight trains came and went. Nowadays, traces of that era are fading, but I feel like I can definitely feel the vibrancy and liveliness of those days in the appearance of the station building. Ekiben has the famous □□, which soothes the fatigue of your journey.

Yasuda. Under the blue sky, the San'in Main Line continues to extend calmly but powerfully to the west today. This railway that runs along the Sea of ​​Japan was once a major artery that supported people's lives and carried logistics. Even now, the city still retains the vestiges of the good old days, and from the train window you can see the rugged yet beautiful coastline and the vibrant lives of its people.

For example, areas that once flourished as coal mines have now transformed into quiet mountain villages. However, once you get off at the station, you can see the warm smiles and unchanging humanity of the people who live there. Local specialties such as fresh seafood and mountain delicacies also make your trip even more enjoyable.

The history that this railway has carved, and the future that will be created in the future. It allows you to experience both.

Hojo. There was once a Japanese National Railways (formerly Japanese National Railways) station in this area, which opened in 1899. It is a key point where the Sanyo Main Line and its branch line, the JR West Kakogawa Line, branch off, and the scene that comes to mind is that many passengers and goods were passing through it. The station building itself is said to have retained a strong Showa-era flavor, so it's heart-warming to think back to the past.

Currently, passenger operations have been relocated to Kakogawa Station, but I feel that the remnants of the once-bustling station are still alive in this area of ​​Hojo. When you come into contact with the history of the area around the station and the activities of the people who once supported its bustle, you realize that the railway was not just a means of transportation, but a history itself deeply connected to the region.

Echigo Hirota. It was once the terminal station on the Echigo Kotsu Tochio Line, supporting local life and transporting people, and is a place that quietly tells the story of its history. In the Showa era, when the railroad still extended to this station, what kind of people and what kind of feelings did they have when they got off at this station? Inside the station building, there must have been a mixture of lively voices, the sadness of departure, and nostalgia for one's hometown. Although the line is now abandoned and the tracks remain, the memories of the bustle that once existed here are still alive in the atmosphere of this quiet station. The excitement of those days, the smiles of people, and the dreams that trains carried... Even today, we can still feel that warm scenery.

Long bird. It was the height of spring, the season when the fresh greenery was dazzling, and I boarded a train aimlessly. Our destination is a mountain town that once boasted prosperity but is now quiet. The green carpet flowing through the train window soothes the hearts of those who see it. Every time I stop at a small station on the way, the station staff greet me with a refreshing greeting that makes me want to straighten up as well. You can feel the warmth of the people and the unchanging activities that are still alive there.

This town once flourished as a mining industry and was visited by many people. The station is decorated with old photographs that remind us of the bustling times of the past, quietly telling the story of its history. In front of the station, there was a lively market selling local specialties, and it was lively. The famous Gohei mochi had a fragrant miso aroma that whet the appetite and soothed the fatigue of the trip.

As I stepped onto the station platform, the cool air caressed my skin. The sound of birds singing from the distant mountains and the sound of plants swaying in the wind. Everything brings you a peaceful time away from the hustle and bustle of the city. When you immerse yourself in this silence, you completely forget about your daily worries.

Tsukayama. When you visit this place, you will feel an indescribable feeling of nostalgia. Once upon a time, this area was filled with the sound of the powerful whistles of steam locomotives and the bustle of freight trains that supported people's lives. When you stop at a station, you are not just a passing point, but a ``crossroads of time'' where people's encounters, farewells, and hopes intertwine. Ekiben is imbued with the rustic flavors of this region, making the journey even deeper.

Tsukayama. This station, which once played an important role in supporting local industry, has changed its appearance with the passage of time. However, the old timetables left in the corner of the station building and the old photos hung on the walls remind us of the bustle of the past. The surrounding scenery also evokes a somewhat nostalgic feeling for those who know the bustle of the past. Lately, I've heard that special trains are sometimes operated to coincide with local festivals, and I can feel that efforts are being made to convey the history and charm of this railway to younger generations.

Tsukayama. When you get off at this station, the first thing that catches your eye is a somewhat tranquil landscape with the surrounding mountains in the background. In the past, the railways that ran through these mountains were an essential lifeline for people's lives. The structure of the station also tells us about the needs of its users at the time, and the remains of the freight platform give us an idea of ​​the great role it played. Nowadays, souvenir shops selling local products from around the station are lined up, providing visitors with the taste and warmth of the area.

Tsukayama. There is a history that the local economy was once enriched by the transportation of mineral resources based on this station. Around the station, there are buildings that still retain traces of those days and what can be called railway heritage, which stirs the imagination of visitors. If you listen to the stories of the local people, you will hear many stories related to the railway, and you will get a sense that the history of this land and the lives of its people have been woven together with the railway. Recently, I've heard that nostalgic railway goods are being sold at cafes in renovated station buildings.

Tsukayama. I believe that this station is not only a railway stop, but also a witness to the history and culture of this area. In the past, many people used this station to write their own stories of life. If you take a walk around the station, you can still see remnants of that time. Recently, as part of regional revitalization efforts, events have begun to be held around the station, creating a new buzz. It makes you feel the warmth of this land as well as the feeling of traveling by train.

Echigo Iwatsuka. Echigo-Iwatsuka Station stands quietly in this land that once prospered as one of Japan's leading rice producers. During the Showa era, this station was bustling with people coming and going, and supported the development of the region as a keystone of the Hokuetsu Railway, later the Echigo Railway, and the current JR Yahiko Line. Although the station building is simple, it retains a Showa era feel that gives you a nostalgic feel, and as you pass through the ticket gate, you can almost feel the scent of arroz (rice) wafting through the air. In the surrounding area, you can feel the vestiges of a time when it once flourished as a rice-producing area, and the old shops and warehouses quietly tell the story of the history of this area. Even now, new rice grown with great care by local people is lined up in front of the station, pleasing the eyes of visitors. When you experience the atmosphere of Echigo-Iwatsuka Station, you are reminded of the vibrancy of the Showa era, the lives of people that have continued since then, and the great role that railways have played.

Raigoji Temple. This is where my journey begins. There is something nostalgic about the appearance of this station, which once served as the starting point of the Echigo Kotsu Tochio Line and also served as a key point connecting with the Shinetsu Main Line, supporting the movement of many people. There are still shopping streets around the station that remind you of the bustle of the past, and every time you walk through the area, you feel like you're suddenly reminded of the Showa era. What is particularly noteworthy is that this area is also said to be the birthplace of the ``uta voice cafe,'' and as a traveler who is sensitive to sound, I can strongly feel the cultural depth of this area. Although there is no ekiben, the scent of a locally loved soba restaurant wafts through the air, and it has more than enough charm to satisfy your travel hunger.
product_ja:
朝日酒造 久保田 萬寿（純米大吟醸）
来迎寺の静かな街並みの中に蔵を構える、日本を代表する名門・朝日酒造。その最高峰が「萬寿」です。華やかな香りと、重厚ながらも一切の雑味がないクリアな旨味。一口含めば、越後の雪解け水のように澄み切った味わいが、心に深く染み渡ります。特別な日の晩酌にふさわしい、日本酒の歴史を刻む一本です。
product_en:
Asahi Sake Brewery Kubota Manju (Junmai Daiginjo)
Asahi Sake Brewery, one of Japan's most prestigious breweries, is located in the quiet streets of Raigoji Temple. The highest peak is "Manju". It has a gorgeous aroma and a deep yet clear flavor without any unpleasant tastes. One sip and the taste, as clear as Echigo's melting snow, will be deeply engrained in your heart. This is a bottle that marks the history of Japanese sake and is perfect for a special evening drink.
product_fr:
Brasserie de saké Asahi Kubota Manju (Junmai Daiginjo)
Asahi Sake Brewery, l'une des brasseries les plus prestigieuses du Japon, est située dans les rues calmes du temple Raigoji. Le plus haut sommet est « Manju ». Il a un arôme magnifique et une saveur profonde mais claire sans aucun goût désagréable. Une gorgée et le goût, aussi clair que la neige fondante d'Echigo, sera profondément ancré dans votre cœur. C'est une bouteille qui marque l'histoire du saké japonais et qui est parfaite pour un verre spécial en soirée.
product_tw:
朝日清酒釀酒廠久保田饅頭（純米大吟釀）
朝日清酒釀酒廠是日本最負盛名的啤酒廠之一，位於來迎寺安靜的街道上。最高峰是「滿洲」。它具有華麗的香氣和深沉而清澈的味道，沒有任何令人不快的味道。喝一口，那味道就像越後融化的雪一樣清澈，會深深地刻在你的心裡。這是一瓶標誌著日本清酒歷史的瓶子，非常適合作為特殊的晚間飲品。

text_en: Maekawa. This is a journey that takes you back to the days when steam locomotives of the Showa era ran, spewing smoke. For example, 〇〇 station was once a bustling place. Although there are few people around now, I feel that the station building is engraved with memories of the prosperity of the past. In front of the station, there is a specialty called 〇〇, which has been loved by locals for a long time, and it warms the stomachs of travelers and at the same time gives them a sense of the local climate. Recently, a new event called 〇〇 has been held, and the area is said to be crowded with young people. I hope that you will be able to see a landscape where you can feel the passage of time, but where the unchanging humanity and history of railways are still alive.

Nagaoka. This town, which represents Echigoji, flourished as a post town in ancient times, and in recent years has become famous throughout the country for its large fireworks display, making it a veritable intersection of beauty and history. This station, which serves the Shin-Etsu Main Line, the Joetsu Shinkansen, and the local line, Koshino Shu*Kura, is a key point that continues to support the movement of people. Around the station, there are remnants of former military facilities and a spacious space reminiscent of the majestic flow of the Shinano River, allowing you to forget the hustle and bustle of the city for a while. The ekiben is lined with delicacies from Echigo, such as bamboo dumplings and hegi soba, and is sure to deepen the joy of your trip. Every time I visit this town, I think of the smoke spewed out by the Showa era steam locomotives and the vibrancy of the people.

Niitsu Station. Since its opening in 1899, it has been a glorious hub that has led Japan's modernization as a railway town where the Shin-Etsu, Banetsu, and Uetsu lines intersect. Since the days when steam locomotives filled the huge yards, the city has continued to flourish as a base for rolling stock manufacturing, and is a symbol of the pride of the railway kingdom.

Kyogase Station. It started life as a signal station in 1944, and is a key agricultural hub located in the middle of the vast Echigo Plain, which supported food shortages after the war. From the window of the train that runs through the Koshihikari Sea, which is nurtured by the rich waters of the Agano River, you can feel the strength of the farming village that has carved out a history of pioneering.

Suwon station. Since its opening in 1919, it has supported the local culture as the gateway to the former Suwon Magistrate's Office and Hyoko Lake, which is known as a visiting place for swans. The weight of its history, as it was once the prefectural capital of Suwon Prefecture after the abolition of the feudal domain in the Meiji era, can be felt quietly from the quiet streetscape in front of the station.

Kamiyama station. This station, which was upgraded from a signal station in 1944 and is surrounded by peaceful countryside, is a place that still reminds us of the hardships of passing in the wrong direction during the single-track era of the Uetsu Main Line. It is now an unmanned station, but when you stand on the platform you can see the Gozu Mountain Range in the distance, allowing you to experience the changing seasons of Echigo.

Tsukioka station. Since its opening in 1919, it has welcomed many visitors to enjoy its hot springs as a railway gateway to Tsukioka Onsen, which boasts one of the highest levels of sulfur content in Japan. When you think of the hustle and bustle of horse-drawn carriages and buses that supported the bustle of the hot spring town in the early Showa era, you can feel the deep connection between the blessings of the land and the railway that nurtured these famous hot springs.

Nakaura Station. It is a place with a simple appearance that has a history of being opened as a signal station in 1944 and then being upgraded to a station to support regional development after the war. Even though the city of Shibata is approaching, the scenery of rice fields that continues to spread out shows that the Uetsu Main Line has been a rice road since ancient times.

Shibata Station. It opened in the first year of the Taisho era, and has a beautiful white-walled station building that represents the prestige of the castle town of Shibata, making it one of the most important locations in the Joetsu region. It once branched off from the Akaya Line, and has a history of serving as a military capital and developing commerce, and the sound of trains that still echoes through the platforms today symbolizes the pride of this historic town.
product_ja:
菊水酒造「ふなぐち一番しぼり」
城下町・新発田が世界に誇る、日本初の「生原酒缶」。一切の加水や加熱をせず、絞りたての瑞々しさと19度という力強いコクをそのまま封じ込めています。フレッシュな果実のような香りが鼻を抜け、どっしりとした旨味が喉を駆け抜ける快感。新発田の冬の厳しさと、蔵人の情熱が弾ける「越後の生んだ魔法の缶」です。
product_en:
Kikusui Sake Brewery “Funaguchi Ichiban Shibori”
Japan's first "raw unprocessed sake can", which the castle town of Shibata is proud of to the world. Without adding any water or heating, we preserve the freshness of freshly squeezed sake and the powerful richness of 19 degrees Celsius. A pleasant sensation of fresh fruit-like scent passing through your nose and a rich flavor running down your throat. This is a ``magic can from Echigo'' that captures the harshness of Shibata's winters and the passion of the brewers.
product_fr:
Brasserie de saké Kikusui « Funaguchi Ichiban Shibori »
La première « boîte de saké brut non transformé » du Japon, dont la ville fortifiée de Shibata est fière auprès du monde entier. Sans ajout d'eau ni chauffage, nous préservons la fraîcheur du saké fraîchement pressé et la puissante richesse de 19 degrés Celsius. Une agréable sensation de parfum fruité frais passant par le nez et une saveur riche coulant dans la gorge. Il s'agit d'une « canette magique d'Echigo » qui capture la rigueur des hivers de Shibata et la passion des brasseurs.
product_tw:
菊水酒造“船口一番絞”
城下町柴田引以為傲的日本首個「未加工的清酒罐頭」。無需添加任何水或加熱，我們就能保留鮮榨清酒的新鮮度和 19 攝氏度的濃鬱口感。新鮮水果般的香氣穿過您的鼻子，濃鬱的味道流過您的喉嚨，令人愉悅。這是一款“來自越後的魔罐”，捕捉了柴田嚴冬的嚴酷和釀酒師的熱情。

text_en: Kaji station. Since its opening in 1912, it has been loved by many cherry blossom viewing visitors as the gateway to the rows of cherry blossom trees in full bloom along the banks of the Kaji River. It was once a point of contact for logistics using the river's currents, and the scent of flowers carried on the spring breeze evokes memories of the rich seasons brought by the railways.

Kanazuka Station. Since its opening in 1912, it has quietly passed the time as a simple relay point connecting the surrounding rich rural areas and the city of Shibata. The appearance of the old platform, which witnessed the wave of agricultural reform and mechanization in the Showa era, provides peace of mind to travelers as part of the unchanged rural landscape of Echigo.

Nakajo Station. Since its opening in 1919, it has been the central hub of Tainai City, supporting agriculture nurtured by the underground water of the former Tainai River and post-war industrial development. With a history of flourishing as a post town on the Oshu Kaido, the town has now been reborn as a modern station building, but the town's spirit of preserving the tradition of handicrafts is still alive and well.

Hirakida station. Since its opening in 1912, it has been located at the northern edge of the Echigo Plain, on the border of the mountain range, and has continued to watch over the harsh snowy landscape of winter. There was a time when it was a thriving distribution center for lumber and agricultural products, and when you step off the platform, you can feel the smell of the earth and feel the history of the railway.

Sakamachi station. Since its opening in 1912, it has supported the history of the railway, serving as a junction with the Yonezaka Line that continues towards Yamagata, and as a key point for operation with a locomotive depot. During the heyday of steam locomotives in the early Showa era, many railway workers lived in this town, and the proud memories of it being a vibrant railway fortress have been passed down to this day.

Hirabayashi Station. This station, which was built in 1950 at the request of the local community during the post-war reconstruction period, is a peaceful place surrounded by rich orchards and countryside. You can feel that the convenience brought by the new railway and the passion of the local residents who responded to it have blended into the calm atmosphere of the current station building.

Iwafunecho Station. Since its opening in 1912, it has served as the railway entrance to the historic Iwafune Port facing the Sea of ​​Japan, and has been accompanied by the aroma of seafood. In the past, fish unloaded from the port were shipped from here to all over the country, and it has a glorious history as a vibrant logistics hub where the bounty of the sea and land railways intersected.

Murakami station. Since its opening in 1912, it has maintained a dignified appearance as the face of Murakami, a castle town with a culture of salmon and the aroma of tea. Even before the wave of electrification arrived in the early Showa period, this station had a heavy responsibility as the entrance to Ou, and the station building, which still harmonizes with the black-walled townscape, conveys the pride of samurai culture to travelers.
product_ja:
村上名産「塩引鮭（しおびきざけ）」
「鮭のまち」村上の冬を彩る、寒風が育む芸術品。雄鮭と塩のみを使い、伝統の「吊り下げ」技法で熟成させた身は、旨味が極限まで凝縮されています。焼けば皮はパリッと香ばしく、身からは濃厚な熟成香が溢れ出します。これぞ白いご飯の最高のご馳走。村上の歴史ある街並みを吹き抜ける「鮭の風」を味わうような体験です。
product_en:
Murakami's specialty "Shiobiki salmon"
Murakami, the city of salmon, is a work of art nurtured by the cold winds that colors the winter. Using only male salmon and salt, the meat is aged using the traditional ``hanging'' technique, and the flavor is concentrated to the utmost. When grilled, the skin becomes crispy and fragrant, and the meat exudes a rich aroma of ripeness. This is the best white rice treat. It is an experience like enjoying the ``Salmon Wind'' blowing through the historic streets of Murakami.
product_fr:
Spécialité de Murakami "Saumon Shiobiki"
Murakami, la ville du saumon, est une œuvre d'art nourrie par les vents froids qui colorent l'hiver. Utilisant uniquement du saumon mâle et du sel, la viande est vieillie selon la technique traditionnelle de la « suspension » et la saveur est concentrée au maximum. Lorsqu'elle est grillée, la peau devient croustillante et parfumée, et la viande dégage un riche arôme de maturité. C'est la meilleure friandise au riz blanc. C'est une expérience comme profiter du « vent de saumon » soufflant dans les rues historiques de Murakami.
product_tw:
村上的名產“鹽引鮭魚”
村上是鮭魚之城，是冬季冷風孕育的藝術品。僅使用雄性鮭魚和鹽，並採用傳統的「懸掛」技術進行熟成，將風味濃縮到極致。烤的時候，皮變得酥脆香濃，肉散發著濃鬱的成熟香氣。這是最好的白米飯。這就像享受吹過村上歷史悠久的街道的“鮭魚風”一樣的體驗。

text_en: Majima Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has continued to attract travelers as the entrance to the spectacular view of the Sea of ​​Japan after passing through the town of Murakami. The railway, which was laid along the coastline where the rough waves were crashing against it, is a reminder of the tenacity of our predecessors who overcame the difficult construction work of the Showa era and the memories of the people who lived in harmony with the sea.

Echigo-Hayakawa Station. Since its opening in 1923, it has been a place that heralds the beginning of the Sasagawa River, and has watched over the ruggedness and beauty of the coastline lined with strangely shaped rocks. You can feel the history of railways vividly coloring local life, once serving as a means of transport for small fishing villages and as a place of relaxation for summer travelers visiting the seaside.

Kuwagawa Station. Since its opening in 1923, it has been located at the heart of the scenic Sasagawa Nagare, and has captured the hearts of many travelers with its beautiful sunset over the sea. The sight of the blue sea, white sandy beaches, and trains running along the shore, unchanged since the Showa era, makes you feel that the railway is a work of art that captures the original scenery of the Sea of ​​Japan.

Imagawa station. This place, which was opened as a signal station in 1944 and upgraded to a station after the war, is surrounded by the overwhelming power of the Sea of ​​Japan that stretches out in front of you. The station building standing resolutely next to a quiet fishing port, exposed to the sea breeze, is a testament to the indomitable spirit of the people who have continued to protect the railway in a harsh natural environment.

Echigo Samukawa Station. Since opening in 1923, we have been a veteran of history, having faced the harsh waves of the Sea of ​​Japan head-on, with blizzards flying up in the winter. It gives us a deep sense of how the railways used to transport goods from here to mountain villages, overcoming rugged terrain, and were the bonds that kept the lives of the region together.

Katsuki station. Since its opening in 1923, it has been located between steep cliffs where mountains fall into the sea, and has become a strategic point where the national highway and railway run side by side. This area, which has long been a difficult point for the highway connecting Echigo and Dewa, can be seen in modern times, with the railway running smoothly through it, showing us both the progress of the times and the unchanging majesty of nature.

Fuya Station. It opened in 1923 as the northernmost station in Niigata Prefecture, and has seen off travelers crossing the prefectural border with Yamagata Prefecture, making it the very last stop in Kaetsu. It was once a base for steam locomotives to connect auxiliary machines and tackle difficult terrain, and when you look at the tracks that continue north from the end of the platform, you can feel the continuation of the epic railway journey that crossed the border.

Nezugaseki Station. Since its opening in 1922, it is the southernmost gateway in Yamagata Prefecture, conveying the history of "Nenju-seki" that separated Echigo and Dewa to the present day. Legend has it that Yoshitsune once passed through this place when he fled to Oshu, and even today, it gently embraces the romance of travelers who cross prefectural borders with the sea breeze.

Koiwakawa Station. This station, which was opened as a signal station in 1944 and upgraded after the war, is the gateway to a quiet fishing village that clings to the rugged coastline. The rough waves of the Sea of ​​Japan that can be seen from the platform still speak to us through the sound of the waves, echoing the tenacity of our predecessors when the railroad once carved out this difficult area.

Atsumi Onsen Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has served as the entrance to the famous Atsumi Onsen, and has gracefully welcomed literary figures, artists, and many spa visitors. It still retains the memory of the glory that famous trains such as the limited express ``Nihonkai'' ran through, and it still maintains an elegant appearance as a gorgeous base for sightseeing in Shonai.
product_ja:
温海（あつみ）名産 赤かぶ漬
開湯千二百年を誇る名湯の地で、古くから伝わる「焼畑農法」で育てられた赤かぶ。その鮮やかな紅色は、添加物を使わず酢と塩だけで引き出された自然の輝きです。パリッ、ポリッとした小気味よい食感と共に、かぶ本来のほろ苦さと甘酸っぱさが口を清めてくれます。温泉宿の朝食を思い出す、素朴ながらも凛とした山形の味です
product_en:
Atsumi specialty red turnip pickles
Red turnips are grown using the traditional slash-and-burn farming method in a famous hot spring area that has been open for 1200 years. Its bright red color is a natural glow brought out using only vinegar and salt without using any additives. Along with the crunchy, chewy texture, the turnip's natural bitterness and sweet-sour taste will cleanse your mouth. A simple yet dignified taste of Yamagata that reminds me of breakfast at a hot spring hotel.
product_fr:
Cornichons de navet rouge spécialité Atsumi
Les navets rouges sont cultivés selon la méthode traditionnelle de culture sur brûlis dans une célèbre zone de sources chaudes ouverte depuis 1 200 ans. Sa couleur rouge vif est un éclat naturel mis en valeur uniquement par du vinaigre et du sel, sans aucun additif. En plus de sa texture croquante et moelleuse, l'amertume naturelle et le goût aigre-doux du navet nettoieront votre bouche. Un avant-goût simple mais digne de Yamagata qui me rappelle le petit-déjeuner dans un hôtel thermal.
product_tw:
渥美特產紅蘿蔔泡菜
紅蘿蔔是在擁有 1200 年歷史的著名溫泉區採用傳統刀耕火種方式種植的。其鮮紅色是僅使用醋和鹽而不使用任何添加劑而呈現的自然光澤。蘿蔔的口感鬆脆耐嚼，天然的苦味和酸甜的味道可以清潔你的口腔。簡單又凝重的山形味道，讓人想起溫泉旅館的早餐。

text_en: Isokawa Station. It opened in 1922 and has served as the only lifeline connecting the village in the rugged terrain where the mountains approach the sea. This station, which suddenly appears between the tunnels that were the result of the civil engineering technology that supported the high economic growth period of the Showa era, is proof that the railroad coexisted with Ou's harsh nature.

Onado Station. This area, which began as a traffic signal station in 1944, still retains the atmosphere of a hidden village tucked away in a cove. There was once a time when peddlers carrying small fish were lively, and as you stood on the platform, the gentle scent of the sea brought back memories of the distant Showa era.

Mise station. Since its opening in 1923, it has prospered as a hub for transporting Shonai's seafood, with a spectacular view of Mise Rock jutting out into the Sea of ​​Japan. With a history of once being a bustling post town, the wave of modernization brought about by the railways is a reminder of a time when this quiet port town was breathed new life into this quiet port town.

Uzen Mizusawa Station. This station, newly built in 1920, is a turning point in your journey, leaving the coastline and entering the vast Shonai Plain. Surrounded by paddy fields, the peaceful landscape reflects the pride of the people of Shonai, who have a long history of rice cultivation, along with the golden ears of rice.

Uzen-Oyama Station. Since its opening in 1919, this historic station has been the gateway to Daisen, one of the leading sake-producing towns in the Tohoku region, and has been accompanied by the scent of new sake. Thinking back to the vibrant days when freight cars loaded with barrels of sake headed across the country, the chimneys of the brewery that still remain today testify to the years when railroads and industry worked together.

Tsuruoka Station. Since its opening in 1919, it has continued to carry a rich history and culture as the face of the Shonai Domain's 140,000 koku castle town. During the transition from the Meiji era to the Showa era, Shonai Kotsu trains once ran through the area, and its character has reigned as a key transportation hub for the region, and its character still shines brightly as the pride of the town.
product_ja:
殿様のだだちゃ豆（冷凍・フリーズドライ）
枝豆の王様、鶴岡特産「だだちゃ豆」。独特の香ばしい香りと、噛むほどに広がる濃厚な甘みは、一度食べたら他の枝豆には戻れないと言われるほど。旬の美味しさを閉じ込めた冷凍品や、贅沢に練り込んだお菓子はお取り寄せでも不動の人気です。庄内平野の豊かな土壌が生んだ、まさに「大地の宝石」をぜひご自宅で。
product_en:
Tonosama's Dadacha beans (frozen/freeze-dried)
Dadacha beans, the king of edamame, are a specialty of Tsuruoka. It has a unique fragrant aroma and a rich sweetness that spreads the more you chew, so much so that once you try it, you won't be able to go back to other edamame. Frozen products packed with seasonal deliciousness and luxuriously kneaded sweets are always popular, even when ordered. Enjoy the ``gems of the earth'' produced by the rich soil of the Shonai plains at home.
product_fr:
Haricots Dadacha de Tonosama (surgelés/lyophilisés)
Les haricots Dadacha, roi des edamame, sont une spécialité de Tsuruoka. Il a un arôme parfumé unique et une riche douceur qui se propage au fur et à mesure que vous mâchez, à tel point qu'une fois que vous l'aurez essayé, vous ne pourrez plus revenir aux autres edamame. Les produits surgelés remplis de délices de saison et les friandises luxueusement pétries sont toujours populaires, même lorsqu'ils sont commandés. Profitez chez vous des « joyaux de la terre » produits par le sol riche des plaines de Shonai.
product_tw:
Tonosama 的 Dadacha 豆（冷凍/冷凍乾燥）
毛豆之王「大茶豆」是鶴岡的特產。它具有獨特的芳香香氣和越嚼越香的濃鬱甜味，以至於一旦嘗試過就再也回不去吃其他毛豆了。充滿時令美味的冷凍食品和奢華的糕點即使在點餐時也總是很受歡迎。在家中即可享受莊內平原肥沃土壤所孕育的「大地寶石」。

text_en: Fujishima station. Established in 1912, it was once the castle town of Fujishima Castle and the center of the fertile Shonai Plain, supporting the modernization of agriculture. The endless flat rice fields surrounding the station quietly tell the story of the history of post-war farming villages, which were enriched by the fertilizer and machinery brought in by the railway.

Nishibukuro station. This station, which was opened as a signal station in 1944, has a simple appearance and is directly exposed to the strong winds blowing through the Shonai Plain. This platform still retains the original scenery of the railway, which was once a part of daily life, where local farmers would wait for the train with their farm produce.

Amarume station. Since its opening in 1919, it has served as the junction with the Rikuu West Line and the "crossroads of Shonai" connecting the inland and the coast. Since the era of steam locomotives in the Showa era, the bustle in front of the station still conveys the memories of the heyday of the railway, when many transiting passengers came and went through this platform, bringing vitality to the town.

Kita Amarume Station. It is an unmanned station with a relatively recent history, having been newly established in 1963 in response to the expansion of farmland and population growth after the war. This place, located next to the railway line that cuts straight through the vast plains, offers the most beautiful views of Mt. Chokai in each season, making it a place of spiritual rest for travelers.

Sunagoe station. Since its opening in 1919, it has prospered as a distribution center for goods located downstream of the Mogami River, and as a gateway to the former Hirata Town. While it retains memories of the days when riverboats and railroads connected the baton of logistics, the sight of it now quietly watching over the countryside gives you a sense of the gentle passage of time.

Higashi Sakata Station. This station, which was opened as a signal station in 1944, is a place that holds memories of the vast train yard just before entering the port town of Sakata. In the past, freight trains were constantly coming and going, and the heartbeat of logistics that supported Japan's high economic growth can still be felt faintly in the echoes of the rails.

Sakata station. Since its opening in 1912, it has supported Japan's modernization as the new logistics heart of the "merchant capital" that flourished with the Kitamaebune fleet. Through the Showa and Heisei eras, the vast grounds still overlooking Mt. Chokai are strongly engraved with the wealth brought by the Mogami River and the history of prosperity built by the railway.
product_ja:
山形県産米「つや姫」（特別栽培米）
炊き上がりの輝き、際立つ粒立ち。酒田が誇る「つや姫」は、口に含んだ瞬間に広がる上品な甘みと、もっちりとした粘りが特徴です。冷めても美味しさが変わらないため、おにぎりや贅沢なお弁当にも最適。鳥海山からの清らかな水と、庄内農家の情熱が結実した、日本一の評価を欲しいままにするブランド米の真髄を味わってください。
product_en:
Yamagata Prefecture rice “Tsuyahime” (specially cultivated rice)
Shine after cooking, outstanding graininess. Sakata's proud ``Tsuyahime'' is characterized by its elegant sweetness that spreads the moment you put it in your mouth, and its chewy consistency. The taste remains the same even when it gets cold, so it's perfect for rice balls and luxurious lunch boxes. Enjoy the essence of a brand of rice that is rated the best in Japan and is the fruit of the pure water from Mt. Chokai and the passion of Shonai farmers.
product_fr:
Riz de la préfecture de Yamagata « Tsuyahime » (riz spécialement cultivé)
Brillance après cuisson, grain exceptionnel. Le fier « Tsuyahime » de Sakata se caractérise par sa douceur élégante qui se propage dès que vous le mettez dans votre bouche, et par sa consistance moelleuse. Le goût reste le même même lorsqu'il fait froid, il est donc parfait pour les boulettes de riz et les boîtes à lunch luxueuses. Profitez de l'essence d'une marque de riz classée comme la meilleure au Japon et fruit de l'eau pure du mont Chokai et de la passion des agriculteurs Shonai.
product_tw:
山形縣米「Tsuyahime」（特產米）
煮後光澤，顆粒感突出。坂田引以為傲的「Tsuyahime」的特點是入口即化的優雅甜味和耐嚼的口感。即使冷了味道也不會變，非常適合做菜團和豪華便當。享受日本第一品牌米的精髓，它是鳥海山純淨水和莊內農民的熱情的成果。

text_en: Hontate station. Since its opening in 1919, it has continued to support the lives of the local community as a link to the rich granary region located on the north side of Sakata. As you look north from the platform, the majestic sight of Mt. Chokai looms larger and larger, giving the impression that it is quietly foretelling the difficult journey that is about to take place across the prefectural border.

Minamichokai station. This station, which was born in 1952 with the post-war pioneering spirit still alive, is, as its name suggests, a sacred place where you can get the closest view of Dewa Fuji and Mt. Chokai. The harmony between the rural landscape, nurtured by pure spring water, and the divine appearance of the mountains makes it feel like one of the most luxurious landscapes ever brought to you by railways.

Yusa Station. Since opening in 1919, we have lived alongside rich nature as the gateway to the ``village of water'' located at the foot of Mt. Chokai. The station was once a popular climbing point for mountain worshipers, and the history of many pilgrims landing at this station is still alive today in the pure air that hangs over the station building.

Fukiura Station. Since its opening in 1919, it has served as a temple town for Chokaisan Omonoki Shrine and as an entrance to the rugged coastline, attracting many travelers. In the past, this area holds memories of the difficult part of railways, where trains that braved the steep mountain pass from here north to the border of Akita Prefecture panted powerfully as they battled the sea breeze.

Mega station. It was opened in 1944 as a signal station, and as the last station in Yamagata Prefecture, it stands on the prefectural border with Akita, giving it the feel of an unexplored region. Located on a small piece of flat land between the mountains and the sea, just before the tunnel that crosses the prefectural border, it has been quietly watching over the safety of the journey, making it the hidden guardian of the Uetsu Main Line.

Kosagawa Station. Since its opening in 1920, it has been the southernmost station in Akita Prefecture, welcoming travelers crossing the prefectural border with the sound of the ocean waves. The winding railway that continues along the coastline still quietly tells the story of the history when steam locomotives once crossed the foothills of Mt. Chokai.

Kamihama station. It was founded in 1923 as the terminal station of the Uetsu-Kita Line, and was once a thriving base for the extension construction going south from here. Its appearance, surrounded by calm countryside and the sea, conveys to this day the peace of the railway that survived the turbulent Showa era.

Nigata Station. Since its opening in 1920, it has served as a gateway to a scenic spot loved by Matsuo Basho, delivering the romance of history to many travelers. Looking out the train window at the Kujukushima Islands, which were uplifted by the great earthquake of 1804, makes you feel the weight of the years that the wonders of nature and railways have coexisted.
product_ja:
にかほ産 いぶりがっこ（奥瀬のいぶり）
かつて芭蕉が愛した名勝・象潟。この地で冬の焚き火の煙に燻されて作られる「いぶりがっこ」は、秋田の冬の結晶です。楢や桜の木で燻された大根の力強い香ばしさと、パリッとした食感、そして噛むほどに溢れる野菜の甘み。お取り寄せならチーズを添えて洋風に楽しむのも乙なもの。秋田の囲炉裏の風景が目に浮かぶ、郷愁の味です。
product_en:
Iburigakko from Nikaho (Okuse no Iburi)
Zogata is a scenic spot that was once loved by Basho. ``Iburigakko'', which is made here by smoking in the smoke of winter bonfires, is the fruit of Akita's winter. The strong aroma of the daikon radish smoked over oak and cherry wood, the crispy texture, and the sweetness of the vegetables that overflow as you chew. If you order it, you can enjoy it Western-style by adding cheese. It is a nostalgic taste that brings to mind the scenery of an Akita hearth.
product_fr:
Iburigakko de Nikaho (Okuse no Iburi)
Zogata est un endroit pittoresque autrefois apprécié par Basho. L'« Iburigakko », fabriqué ici en fumant dans la fumée des feux de joie hivernaux, est le fruit de l'hiver d'Akita. L'arôme puissant du radis daikon fumé au bois de chêne et de cerisier, la texture croustillante et la douceur des légumes qui débordent à la mastication. Si vous le commandez, vous pourrez le déguster à l'occidentale en ajoutant du fromage. C'est un goût nostalgique qui rappelle le décor d'un foyer d'Akita.
product_tw:
來自仁賀保的 Iburigakko（Okuse no Iburi）
佐方是芭蕉曾經喜愛的風景名勝。在冬季篝火的煙霧中熏製而成的“煙熏”是秋田冬季的果實。用橡木和櫻桃木熏過的蘿蔔的濃鬱香氣，酥脆的口感，咀嚼時溢出的蔬菜的甜味。如果點的話，可以加入芝士，享受西式風味。這是讓人想起秋田爐邊風景的懷舊味道。

text_en: Gimpo Station. Since its opening in 1920, the town has lived with the vibrancy of the fishing town, and has carried the pride of being the hometown of Antarctic explorer Shirase Yasu. The area in front of the station was once a busy place for the shipping of lumber and seafood, and there are strong vestiges of the days when the railway was the main artery that supported local life.

Nikaho Station. When it first opened in Taisho 11, it was called Tatemachi Station, but later inherited the name as the center of the region, and has progressed along with the development of the electronic parts industry. The vast site overlooking Mt. Chokai still conveys the memories of an industry that was once frequented by many commuters and freight trains.

Nishime Station. Since its opening in 1920, this area of ​​vast reclaimed land and sand dunes has functioned as a base to support the modernization of agriculture. The sight of a train gliding through the beautiful countryside that was developed in the Showa era symbolizes the rich history of this area.

Ugohonjo Station. It opened in 1923, and has continued to support local transportation as a connection point with the Yuri Kogen Railway, while maintaining the dignity of the former castle town. From transporting lumber in the early Showa era to commuting to work and school today, the constant flow of people is a testament to the strength of the town of Honjo.
product_ja:
由利牛（ゆりぎゅう）ステーキ・すき焼きセット
秋田県南西部の広大な牧草地で育てられる「由利牛」。きめ細やかな霜降りと、口の中でとろけるような脂の軽やかさが特徴の黒毛和牛です。焼けばナッツのような甘い香りが立ち込め、一口噛めば濃厚な赤身の旨味が弾けます。由利高原の清風と、鳥海山の恵みが育んだ秋田の至宝。特別な食卓を彩る、最高級の肉体験をお約束します。
product_en:
Yuri beef steak/sukiyaki set
Yuri beef is raised on vast pastures in southwestern Akita Prefecture. Kuroge Wagyu beef is known for its fine marbling and light fat that melts in your mouth. When grilled, it emits a sweet, nutty aroma, and when you bite into it, you can feel the rich flavor of the red meat. A treasure of Akita, nurtured by the fresh breeze of Yuri Plateau and the blessings of Mt. Chokai. We promise you the highest quality meat experience that will brighten up your special dining table.
product_fr:
Ensemble steak de bœuf/sukiyaki Yuri
Le bœuf Yuri est élevé sur de vastes pâturages dans le sud-ouest de la préfecture d'Akita. Le bœuf Kuroge Wagyu est connu pour son persillage fin et son gras léger qui fond dans la bouche. Lorsqu'il est grillé, il dégage un arôme sucré de noisette, et lorsque vous le mordez, vous pouvez sentir la riche saveur de la viande rouge. Un trésor d'Akita, nourri par la brise fraîche du plateau de Yuri et les bénédictions du mont Chokai. Nous vous promettons une expérience de viande de la plus haute qualité qui égayera votre table à manger spéciale.
product_tw:
尤里牛排/壽喜燒套餐
尤里牛肉在秋田縣西南部廣闊的牧場上飼養。黑毛和牛以其細膩的大理石花紋和入口即化的輕質脂肪而聞名。烤的時候散發出甜甜的堅果香氣，咬下去就能感受到紅肉的濃郁香味。由利高原的清風和鳥海山的恩惠孕育而成的秋田之寶。我們承諾為您提供最優質的肉類體驗，為您的特殊餐桌增添光彩。

text_en: Ishiwaki signal station. It was established in 1974 when the railway was double-tracked, and has been a key point in the operation of the Koyoshi River, quietly watching over the safety of trains crossing the bridge. The heartbeat of the railroad's heyday, when steam locomotives once spewed smoke and heavy freight trains crisscrossed the area, can still be heard mixed in with the sound of the rails.

Ugo Iwatani Station. Since its opening in 1922, it has played an important role as a gateway for journeys across the Dewa Hills and as a logistics base for surrounding rural areas. The atmosphere of the station building, which was rebuilt during the period of high economic growth in the Showa era, retains the warmth of being a spiritual station where many people departed for the city and returned.

Orito Station. It was opened as a signal station in Taisho 11, and after making history as a difficult place to cross a steep mountain pass, it was upgraded to a station with privatization. The appearance of this unexplored area, surrounded by forest, silently tells us how the Uetsu Main Line carved out and connected the rugged nature.

Ugo Kameda Station. Since its opening in 1919, it has been filled with a deep atmosphere, being known as the entrance to the former castle town of the Kameda clan and as the setting for the masterpiece ``Sand Vessel.'' The scenery in front of the station, which seems to have frozen the quiet time of the Showa era, makes you feel that the stories brought to you by railways are still alive in this area.

Iwaki Minato Station. This new station on the Uetsu Main Line, opened in 2001, is creating new vitality in the area through collaboration with roadside stations. It symbolizes the modern history of railways, from when they were just a means of transportation to when they became attractive destinations.

Michikawa Station. Since its opening in 1919, this location overlooking the Sea of ​​Japan has carved out scientific history as the birthplace of domestic rockets. The scenery of the railway stretching towards the blue sky and the sea makes us feel the passion of our predecessors who ventured into the unknown, and the hope for the future that the railway has connected them with.

Shimohama station. Since its opening in 1919, it is the closest healing station to the sea, and has been engraved with sea breezes and memories of summers filled with beachgoers. If you think back to the summer holidays of the Showa era, when special trains were running and the cheers of children filled the platform, you can feel the years that railways have carried people's memories.

Katsurane Station. It began life as a signal station in 1962, and was elevated to a station after years of hard work at the site that supported the miscommunication of trains. Even as you feel the city of Akita approaching, the overwhelming force of the Sea of ​​Japan spreading out below the cliffs signals the climax of your trip on the Uetsu Main Line.

Araya station. Since its opening in 1919, it has been a driving force in the development of southern Akita as a town with the scent of sake brewing and a logistics base that supports a vast paper mill. The vitality of the days when dedicated lines stretched in all directions and freight trains were the very heartbeat of the city can still be seen in the stately streets surrounding the station.

Akita station. Since its opening in 1902, it has been the heart of the capital of Ushu and the final stop on the Uetsu Main Line, making it a sacred place that has completed many journeys and histories. It was once the site of a locomotive depot, and the memories of its glory dominating Tohoku's railways have been passed down through the generations as a pride as a railway town, even in today's modern and lively station buildings.
product_ja:
佐藤養助「稲庭うどん」
[紹介文]
羽越本線の終着、秋田。万延元年より受け継がれる「一子相伝」の技が、驚くほど細く、滑らかな麺を生み出します。茹で上がった麺は透き通るような白さを放ち、喉を通る瞬間の心地よさはもはや芸術の域。お取り寄せのギフトセットなら、自宅で料亭の味が再現できます。秋田の凛とした冬の空気を感じる、気品あふれる一杯です。
product_en:
Yosuke Sato “Inaniwa Udon”
[Introduction]
Akita is the last stop on the Uetsu Main Line. The ``Ichiko Souden'' technique passed down from the first year of Manen produces surprisingly thin and smooth noodles. The boiled noodles have a crystal-clear white color, and the moment they go down your throat, the comfort is like an art. If you order a gift set, you can recreate the taste of a Japanese restaurant at home. A drink full of elegance that lets you feel Akita's dignified winter air.
product_fr:
Yosuke Sato « Inaniwa Udon »
[Présentation]
Akita est le dernier arrêt de la ligne principale Uetsu. La technique « Ichiko Souden » transmise dès la première année de Manen produit des nouilles étonnamment fines et lisses. Les nouilles bouillies ont une couleur blanche cristalline et dès qu'elles descendent dans la gorge, le réconfort est comme un art. Si vous commandez un coffret cadeau, vous pouvez recréer chez vous le goût d’un restaurant japonais. Une boisson pleine d'élégance qui vous fait ressentir l'air digne de l'hiver d'Akita.
product_tw:
佐藤洋介“稻庭乌冬面”
[簡介]
秋田是羽越本线的终点站。從萬年元年傳承下來的「市子總電」技術，可以製作出令人驚奇的細細光滑的麵條。煮好的麵條顏色潔白晶瑩，入喉的那一刻，舒適感就像是一種藝術。如果訂購禮品套裝，您可以在家中重現日式餐廳的風味。充滿優雅氣息的飲品，讓您感受到秋田冬日的端莊氣息。
